articles.title: How the Valkyries and Dream Reflect the WNBA’s Evolution
articles.summary: Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals is Saturday.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The Atlanta Dream held the title of "most recent WNBA expansion franchise" for 16 years. That ended last season, when the Golden State Valkyries entered the league.

But they couldn't have entered the league in any more different circumstances.

When the Dream were introduced in 2008, the WNBA was already struggling to stay afloat. A few of the league's original eight teams had already folded, average league attendance was fewer than 7,500 , and the maximum player salary was $95,000.

They enjoyed early success on court, including three Finals appearances in their first six seasons. But they've been in a deep rebuild over the last decade, failing to win a playoff series since 2016.

But a high-profile ownership change in 2021 has resulted in a complete franchise overhaul.

The team hired Morgan Shaw Parker, who joined the team in 2021 as president and chief operating officer. She told FOS last year that the Dream organization had just seven employees when she signed on. It had about 70 at the beginning of this year.

They also hired GM Dan Padover away from the Las Vegas Aces in 2021, who built this team through the draft (Rhyne Howard, Naz Hillmon) or through trades (Angel Reese, Allisha Gray, Jordin Canada). He has won three Executive of the Year awards, including in 2025.

"I think it starts from the top down," Hillmon, who the Dream drafted in 2022, said Friday of the organization's growth. "When I think about the top, obviously I think about the owners, but I'm also thinking about our GM Dan."

The Dream's transformation is still continuing, most clearly seen by the recent struggle to secure 17,000-seat State Farm Arena for their home Finals games. But it's par for the course for one of the last remaining independent franchises in the WNBA, a team whose owner owns no other pro sports team, a problem the Valkyries know nothing about.

Golden State arrived in 2025, nearly two decades after Atlanta, with the WNBA enjoying unprecedented momentum, a $3 billion media-rights package kicking in the following year, and an ownership group with the resources and pedigree to make an immediate impact. The Golden State Group brought in the Valkyries, the same organization that runs the Warriors and Chase Center.

But the Valkyries still had to execute, and they did it much faster than even they expected.

Owner Joe Lacob challenged head coach Natalie Nakase to win a title in five years, and has been ahead of schedule since she first donned the purple and black. She dragged a team full of expansion draftees to the playoffs last year, then turned it into a Finals berth in year two.

The Valkyries have also sold out every single home game, and their fans have created an arena atmosphere that's second to none. The organization is the first to record $100 million in annual revenue , and the first WNBA team to be valued at $1 billion by CNBC —despite only being two seasons old.

"The level of investment from the jump was huge," starting point guard Veronica Burton said Friday. "From our ownership, to our front office, to our coaching staff, I think they've set us up for a position to be successful."

The Valkyries' model has been so successful that other expansion franchises actively admit to taking inspiration from them, and team president Jess Smith's name has even been floated around as a commissioner candidate .

On Saturday, the Dream and Valkyries will meet in the WNBA Finals for the first time, bringing together two franchises whose journeys reflect just how much the league has evolved.

For Atlanta, a championship would symbolize a payoff from a lengthy organizational rebuild. For Golden State, a title in its second season would be a feat no other franchise has achieved, cementing them as the best expansion team in league history.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream vs. Golden State Valkyries pick, prediction, odds: Best bets for the WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Our WNBA handicapper gives his take on which team will win the finals, as well as his favorite bets in the series.
articles.body:
The WNBA Finals tip off on Saturday at the Chase Center, as the second-seeded Golden State Valkyries host the No. 4 seed Atlanta Dream.

Both of these teams pride themselves on defense, generating points off turnovers, shooting a high volume of 3-pointers, protecting the rim and emphasizing rebounding. It is very analytically sound basketball and what we commonly see out of the Oklahoma City Thunder and Boston Celtics, so it's not surprising these teams have reached the finals.

Once we knew the teams, there were still two major unknowns for this series that have started to be figured out.

The first was the location of the games, but that has been worked out and the Atlanta Dream will play at State Farm Arena (where the Hawks play), but change the start time of the games to better accommodate the event. I was hoping the games in Atlanta would be moved to Georgia Tech's arena — which is close by and seats only 9,500 fans — as it would create an edge for the Valkyries (which I'm backing in this series). Part of the home-court advantage is the shooters knowing what the lighting looks and feels like and helps set rhythm and depth perception. If Atlanta role players were in a new environment, it would weaken the home-court advantage.

The second unknown is the health status of the Dream's star point guard Allisha Gray. Gray has been dealing with an injury to her ring finger on her left shooting hand. She missed the previous two games against the New York Liberty and then it was reported she had a "small procedure" shortly after. I thought Gray would be out for the series, but now we are seeing videos of her at practice shooting (and making three 3-pointers in a row).

Let's discuss a series, Game 1 and player prop bet to take now for the WNBA Finals.

WNBA Finals: Atlanta Dream (-105) at Golden State Valkyries (-115)

I'm going to lump these two bets into one writeup, because the angle between the series winner and Game 1 winner is highly correlated. I think the Valkyries have a few edges to lean on in this matchup.

Golden State made the finals after series against Jess Sheppard and A'ja Wilson as the opposing bigs, and they made those players play well below their standard. Wilson shot 41.1% for the series, and Sheppard was at 34.8%. That is down from 52.7% and 57.5%, respectively — a major drop in efficiency.

The Dream made the finals on the heels of Angel Reese being the best player on the team and producing a lot offensively. With the combination of Gray probably being less effective with the hand injury (if she plays), and the Valkyries being a dominant defense against opposing bigs, I think the offensive focal points for the Dream will struggle.

Golden State will also put Defensive Player of the Year runner-up Gabby Williams on Rhyne Howard, and size up against Jordin Canada. The Valkyries also have a coaching advantage, as head coach Natalie Nakase is probably the best head coach in the WNBA. She won Coach of the Year last season, and finished second this season. Nakase had eight days to prepare for this series, and that time gap likely creates a bigger edge in game planning. While Atlanta head coach Karl Smesko is very good himself, they operate on different tiers where this edge goes towards the Valkyries.

I am backing the Golden State home-court advantage, coaching advantage, health advantage and defensive advantage for both Game 1 and the series.

Best bets: Valkyries -2.5 in Game 1 and Valkyries -115 to win the series

Player prop: Veronica Burton WNBA Finals MVP (12-1)

The head of the snake for the Valkyries switches off between Veronica Burton and Williams. It has been Williams for the majority of this season and she has gotten the top honors for All-Star, DPOY and All-WNBA team voting. However, she is a new addition this season and it wasn't long ago that Burton was claiming all of those spots. They are a very solid 1-2 punch. The pricing for the WNBA Finals market lists Burton as the fifth-most likely candidate to win MVP, rightfully behind Williams — but she shouldn't also be behind three different Dream players.

This market seems to be overindexing Williams' performance in the playoffs thus far. Williams is averaging 22.7 point per game (up from 14.4 PPG in the regular season), while Burton is down to 9.5 PPG (after averaging 12.2 PPG in the regular season). The playoff sample size is so small (six games), and heavily matchup dependent, so this feels like an overreaction to have them priced so far apart.

Burton could lead the team in scoring, assist, 3-pointers and also be an engine defensively. Buy the dip for Burton to win WNBA Finals MVP.

articles.title: Los Lakers cierran la pretemporada con más sombras que luces
articles.standfirst: Batacazo por 106-126 ante los Nuggets de Jokic (17+6+8) y aumentan las dudas sobre la era Doncic (15+4+2)
articles.summary: Batacazo por 106-126 ante los Nuggets de Jokic (17+6+8) y empiezan a surgir dudas sobre la era Doncic (15+4+2)
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers cerraron la pretemporada con una derrota ante los Denver Nuggets (106-121) que dejó más dudas que certezas. El equipo de JJ Redick terminó con dos victorias y tres derrotas y evidenció que todavía necesita ajustar muchas piezas. Sin LeBron James, el reto es construir un proyecto competitivo alrededor de Luka Doncic, pero las primeras señales invitan a la cautela. El comienzo del partido fue especialmente preocupante. Denver se impuso por 36-22 en el primer cuarto y llegó a disfrutar de 17 puntos de ventaja, aprovechando los errores y la fragilidad defensiva de los angelinos. Los Lakers acabaron con un 42,7% de acierto en tiros de campo y 14 pérdidas de balón. La reacción posterior no bastó para esconder sus problemas ante una defensa intensa. Otra de las sombras está en la protección del aro y la capacidad para competir físicamente. Los Nuggets encontraron demasiadas facilidades cerca de la canasta -Nikola Jokic acabó con 17 puntos, 6 rebotes y 8 asistencias- y castigaron las dificultades de los Lakers para cerrar espacios y controlar el rebote. Walker Kessler, llamado a aportar presencia interior, terminó con seis puntos y seis rebotes. Si no mejoran en defensa, sufrirán ante los rivales más poderosos del Oeste. La salida de LeBron también obliga a Doncic a asumir una responsabilidad todavía mayor. El esloveno terminó con 15 puntos, cuatro rebotes y dos asistencias en 18 minutos, aunque perdió cinco balones. Austin Reaves aportó 19 puntos, pero la conexión entre ambos y el nuevo pívot aún necesita rodaje. JJ Redick tampoco tiene completamente definida su rotación. El entrenador continúa buscando la combinación más equilibrada para acompañar a Doncic y Reaves, mientras las lesiones y las pruebas de pretemporada dificultan la continuidad. "Busco equilibrio en las alineaciones y jugadores que se complementen y encajen entre sí", explicó Redick, según Los Angeles Times. La falta de claridad en los roles y la necesidad de más alternativas para organizar el ataque son cuestiones pendientes. Hubo algunos destellos, con aportaciones interesantes de Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili y Ziaire Williams, pero no suficientes para cambiar el balance general. Los Lakers necesitan reducir las pérdidas, elevar su intensidad defensiva y encontrar una identidad colectiva que vaya más allá del talento de Doncic. La pretemporada no dicta sentencia, pero el equipo angelino llega al inicio oficial con más incógnitas que certezas y la sensación de que la transición tras la marcha de LeBron será más complicada de lo esperado.

articles.title: NBA’s improved Eastern Conference makes Knicks and Nets’ goals more difficult in 2026-27
articles.summary: The defending-champion Knicks and playoff-hopeful Nets are competing for different things. But they do have this in common: Their respective goals will be mo...
articles.body:
The defending-champion Knicks and playoff-hopeful Nets are competing for different things.

But they do have this in common: Their respective goals will be more difficult to accomplish due to a transformed Eastern Conference that should have more contenders and fewer punching bags this season.

"You see what goes on. A lot of teams got better, and it's good," Knicks forward Mikal Bridges said. "Excited for all of the other teams; you love when the competition's high. Who doesn't love that?"

The Knicks remain, at the very least, the co-favorite to win the East after they steamrolled through the conference last postseason en route to their first NBA championship in 53 years.

Outside of the departure of valuable backup Mitchell Robinson , the Knicks bring back virtually the same roster, including their entire starting lineup.

But while the Knicks dominated a weakened East last spring, they should expect more top-end resistance this season.

The star-hunting Philadelphia 76ers added LeBron James and Jaylen Brown to a core already headlined by Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

Whether the new-look Sixers can build chemistry and stay healthy will likely determine their ceiling, but there's championship upside if everything clicks.

"I didn't leave my family [in Los Angeles]," James said, "to lose in the second round."

The Miami Heat acquired two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo in a franchise-altering trade with the Milwaukee Bucks , pairing him with fellow All-Star big man Bam Adebayo to form what should be the NBA's best defensive frontcourt.

The Heat lack depth and playmaking, which means there's a range of outcomes for how their season will go. But betting against a motivated Antetokounmpo probably isn't smart business — nor is discounting the possibility of Pat Riley adding another difference-maker before season's end.

The Detroit Pistons, who won 60 games last season, remain in the mix now that they've finally re-signed All-Star center Jalen Duren after a tense restricted free agency. So do the Boston Celtics, whose data-driven approach and a full season of a healthy Jayson Tatum should allow them to again compete for a high seed, even after trading Brown away.

The Cleveland Cavaliers are always an excellent regular-season team, and they just went to the Eastern Conference Finals.

After finishing as the No. 5 seed, the Toronto Raptors added Kawhi Leonard to a promising young core, while the Indiana Pacers — just one season removed from an NBA Finals berth — should be vastly improved with a healthy Tyrese Haliburton back from a torn Achilles.

So while the Knicks are surefire contenders, the same can be said to varying degrees about the Sixers, Pistons, Heat, Celtics, Cavs, Pacers and Raptors, too.

That's eight teams for six automatic playoff spots right there.

The Knicks will be focused on the top of the bracket as they try to become the NBA's first repeat champions since the 2017-18 Golden State Warriors.

On the other side of the Brooklyn Bridge, the Nets should set their sights on landing a top-10 seed and making the play-in tournament after three consecutive playoff-less seasons.

After tanking the past two years — without a top-five pick to show for it — the Nets are done prioritizing draft capital.

They added multiple veterans, headlined by Julius Randle, to elevate a group featuring Michael Porter Jr. and numerous first- and second-year players, including rookie point guard Mikel Brown Jr., the No. 6 pick in June's draft.

The Nets have a long way to go after winning only 20 games last season, but the Porter-Randle duo should at least set a floor. Breakouts by Brown or a second-year player such as Egor Dëmin would raise the ceiling.

The problem is that cracking the top-10 in the East won't be easy.

In addition to the eight teams mentioned earlier, there are the ascendant Atlanta Hawks, who will be more seasoned after testing the Knicks during last postseason's first-round series.

There are the Orlando Magic, who have made the playoffs three years in a row.

There are the Washington Wizards, who since January have added Trae Young, Anthony Davis and No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybansta in a major talent infusion.

And there are the Charlotte Hornets, who went 44-38 last season but have since traded away go-to LaMelo Ball.

To make the play-in field, the Nets will have to finish better than at least two of the 12 teams mentioned above. That's definitely doable — especially if injuries come into play — but far from a certainty during a season when fewer teams seem poised to tank.

The Nets will have to prove they belong in the play-in mix rather than at the bottom of the standings, where the rebuilding Chicago Bulls and Antetokounmpo-less Bucks might be the only teams with lower outside expectations.

"We're coming in trying to win," Randle said. "It's as simple as that. However we can help give the younger guys experience and confidence and help them fast track … to contribute to winning basketball, that's really all that matters. All I care about, at the end of the day, is winning, and I know that's what those guys care about."
authors: Peter Sblendorio, New York Daily News

articles.title: Timberwolves get major reality check despite LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards pairing from former head coach
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves enter the 2026-27 NBA season with one of the league’s most intriguing backcourts following the acquisition of LaMelo Ball to pair...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves enter the 2026-27 NBA season with one of the league's most intriguing backcourts following the acquisition of LaMelo Ball to pair with Anthony Edwards. However, former NBA head coach Tyrone Corbin believes Minnesota's championship aspirations will ultimately depend on its defense rather than its offensive firepower.

Speaking with Kyle Odegard of NEXTPredict, Corbin expressed confidence in Ball and Edwards developing chemistry but questioned whether the Timberwolves can consistently slow opposing teams.

"They're going to have to get some stops at some point. Offensively, you look at the talent they'll have on the floor in those two guys alone, they're going to be able to score the ball. Do they have enough to figure out how to slow other teams?" Corbin said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"There are some nights you just can't force your will on a team, and defense will save you. With Rudy Gobert anchoring in there I hope it will help some, but they're going to need to stay in front of their guys at some point."

Minnesota finished its preseason with a 3-3 record, including a 133-116 loss to the Chicago Bulls on Friday night.

Despite his defensive concerns, Corbin expects Ball and Edwards to complement each other offensively.

"Easy. They both are dynamic offensive talents. LaMelo can score from anywhere but he can really pass the ball. You have to make sure the guys on the floor with him are looking, because he will throw it from anywhere and get it there."

Tyrone Corbin believes LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards can thrive together

Ball's arrival gives Edwards another established offensive creator capable of generating scoring opportunities for himself and his teammates.

Corbin also believes their personalities will help accelerate the adjustment.

"He is a great, great young man. I think his personality, and the things I hear about Ant's personality, is that they'll mesh pretty quickly, and that talent on the floor will come together."

However, Minnesota faces considerable competition in a Western Conference featuring the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs .

With Gobert anchoring the interior defense, the Timberwolves have an established rim protector. Still, Corbin emphasized that Minnesota's perimeter defenders must provide sufficient resistance to maximize the team's potential.

"They're going to be good, man. To have Edwards there, and then add a kid like LaMelo, and Rudy in the middle. With the way they're going to be able to score, if they can get some stops, they're going to be something to reckon with in the West."

The Timberwolves will begin their regular season Wednesday, Oct. 21, against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat on the road. The matchup tips off at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN, providing Minnesota an early opportunity to demonstrate how its revamped backcourt performs against Eastern Conference competition.

articles.title: Tacko Fall Lands 76ers Contract, Latest Details Revealed in New NBA Rumors Ahead of Season Opener
articles.summary: As NBA teams finalize their rosters with the regular season starting next week, the Philadelphia 76ers are keeping Tacko Fall on a two-way contract.
articles.body:
As NBA teams finalize their rosters with the regular season starting next week, the Philadelphia 76ers are keeping Tacko Fall on a two-way contract.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania , the Sixers are converting Fall's deal to a two-way contract after he originally signed an Exhibit 10 contract in September.

Fall returned to the NBA this summer after spending the past four seasons playing overseas in the Chinese Basketball Association. He spent the 2025-26 campaign with the Ningbo Rockets, averaging 11.2 points and 6.0 rebounds in 38 games.

A hip injury suffered early in training camp prevented Fall from appearing in any of the 76ers' four preseason games.

The Sixers announced on Oct. 1 that Fall was diagnosed with a hip strain and would be reevaluated in two weeks. There has not yet been an official update from the club on his status.

Philadelphia is in need of more center depth going into the regular season. Joel Embiid will start as long as he is healthy. Adem Bona is likely to be the primary backup for head coach Nick Nurse.

Ariel Hukporti, who signed a one-year deal as a free agent this summer, suffered a season-ending injury when he tore his Achilles in a preseason game against the New York Knicks on Oct. 5.

Fall last played in the NBA during the 2021-22 season when he appeared in 11 games with the Cleveland Cavaliers. He played in 37 total games during his original three-season run in the league from 2019 to '22.

A two-way contract allows the 76ers to split Fall's time with the NBA club and their G League affiliate. He also doesn't count against the standard 15-man NBA roster that teams must have finalized by 5 p.m. ET on Monday.

articles.title: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver blindsides Sonics faithful by floating surprise expansion alternative
articles.summary: Adam Silver told NBA owners that Seattle is no longer a lock for expansion, floating Mexico City as an alternative to drive up bid prices.
articles.body: Hold on, Adam Silver said what now? The NBA commissioner informed league owners that Seattle is no longer a "lock" for expansion? That's the word according to a new report from ESPN, and if you're a Seattleite, you just spit out your $9 oat-milk latte. SACRAMENTO MAKES ITS CASE AS MLB'S NEXT EXPANSION CITY, CALLING ITSELF A MARKET TOO BIG TO IGNORE Last March, all 30 of the NBA's owners voted in favor of exploring expansion in Seattle and Las Vegas. The thought was that this would finally lead to a Sonics return after the team left the Emerald City for Oklahoma City in 2008. ESPN's Brian Windhorst was on television telling Seattle fans to get excited. But Friday, Windhorst's latest article left fans exasperated. The acclaimed NBA reporter wrote that while Silver is a "full-go" on expanding to Vegas, Seattle is far from a guarantee. The commissioner reportedly mentioned Mexico City as an expansion alternative in a meeting with the board of governors last month. ROGER GOODELL DETAILS NFL EXPANSION POSSIBILITIES AND A TIMETABLE FOR A FULL SEASON OF INTERNATIONAL GAMES This didn't officially break any promises, but it did seem to violate an unwritten understanding. It was no accident that the aforementioned owners' vote named Vegas and Seattle exclusively. The former is one of the world's foremost entertainment capitals, and the latter has a starving fan base and state-of-the-art venue in Climate Pledge Arena. Just as notably, One Roof Sports — the group spearheading the Sonics' return — recently landed a billionaire backer in Melinda French Gates. Done deal, right? Not so much. At the heart of all this is Silver's attempt to increase franchise values across the league. And right now, the expectation is that bids for a new team in Vegas could exceed $10 billion. Seattle's bids, meanwhile, are expected to be substantially lower, perhaps because the city already has an NBA-ready arena. Prospective owners don't just want revenue from ticket sales and television contracts. They want the money that comes with controlling an arena, too. Luxury suites and premium seating. Concessions and merchandise. Sponsorships and advertising. Naming rights, concerts and other events. But an ownership group outside One Roof Sports wouldn't necessarily have access to those revenue streams without negotiating a deal with the arena's operators. And building another venue would add billions to an already enormous investment — assuming the city would even approve a second NBA arena. That gives One Roof a significant advantage over competing Seattle bidders and little incentive to offer anything close to $10 billion. But Silver has leverage of his own. And that's where Mexico City comes in. LAS VEGAS PRICES SQUEEZE EVERYDAY TRAVELERS AS POPULAR CITY EMBRACES EXPENSIVE MAKEOVER By floating a city south of the border, Silver is saying that the league can go elsewhere. Could it just be posturing to drive up Seattle's bids? Yeah. But Silver has made no promises to Seattle — nor has he committed to adding two teams at once, assuming he adds two at all. This, of course, is driving some people in the Emerald City bonkers. As former Seattle Post-Intelligencer sports columnist Jim Moore posted on X above a picture of Silver: "This s—t is laughable. It never ends. When does Seattle finally say f—k off to this guy?" Understandable reaction. Sonics fans have been jerked around for 18 years. But Silver has a job to do — dirty as it may seem. His responsibility isn't to make things right with Seattle. It's to get the best possible deal for the league's 30 existing owners. And if invoking Mexico City helps him squeeze another billion or two out of a Seattle bidder, don't expect him to apologize. articles.title: Un 'Tigre' anda suelto
articles.standfirst: Andrés Feliz, gran atracción del Real Madrid ante la visita del Surne Bilbao tras firmar dos actuaciones superlativas en la doble jornada de Euroliga
articles.summary: Andrés Feliz, gran atracción del Real Madrid ante la visita del Surne Bilbao tras firmar dos actuaciones superlativas en la doble jornada de Euroliga
articles.body: El Real Madrid recibe este domingo al Surne Bilbao (12.30 h) con la intención de mantenerse invicto (3-0), condición que en esta cuarta jornada sólo ostentan ya ellos, el líder Kosner Baskonia y el Río Breogán. Será un partido en el que Pedro Martínez seguirá dando descanso a algunos de sus fijos de la Euroliga y minutos a los que cuentan menos en ese torneo. Andrés Feliz ha comenzado el curso a un nivel formidable, y será uno de los focos de atención del partido si su entrenador no le 'enjaula' para darle descanso. El 'Tigre' de Guachupita llega tras firmar dos partidos superlativos en la doble jornada de Euroliga, donde es el tercer madridista más valorado en ese torneo (11,8+3,8+4 y 14 de valoración en 19:32 minutos), sólo por detrás de Maledon y Tavares. Y también es tercero en la Liga Endesa (7,5+5+4,5 y 15 de valoración en 22 minutos), tras Maledon y Luwawu-Cabarrot. La semana fantástica de Feliz arrancó el pasado martes en el triunfo madridista en Milán (89-98), donde fue uno de los pilares del primer triunfo blanco a domicilio en la Euroliga al facturar 15 puntos (5/7 t2, 1/2 t3 y 2/2 tl) y 24 de valoración. Pedro Martínez le alabó tras ese triunfo: "Estamos muy contentos con él no solo por su calidad, que está clarísima, sino que lo más importante para nosotros es su mentalidad. Es un chico fantástico que intenta entrenar duro cada día, tiene una gran mentalidad para escuchar a los entrenadores, ganas de mejorar y una mentalidad ganadora; le encanta competir y tiene un gran corazón”. Y el jueves el dominicano lideró el triunfo del Real Madrid ante el ASVEL Villeurbanne (111-92) con 26 puntos (8/11 triples), 4 rebotes, 5 asistencias y 30 créditos de valoración en 25 minutos. "Me siento bien. Sabemos del ritmo que quiere nuestro entrenador y cada día mejoramos y vamos adaptándonos. Gracias a Dios nos van saliendo las cosas bien", dijo tras el encuentro en los micrófonos de Movistar +. El exterior blanco se muestra ilusionado con los pasos adelante que va dando su equipo pese al lógico proceso de acoplamiento que debe afrontar tras incluir con siete fichajes y entrenador nuevo: "Obviamente al principio siempre cuesta un poco adaptarse, pero creemos en el equipo, y en el proyecto. Hay que seguir esa línea, creo que a largo plazo vamos a hacer un gran trabajo"", Sin embargo en esta ocasión su entrenador, Pedro Martínez, optó por no dorarle demasiado la píldora a su pupilo pese a que este le dio argumentos de sobra para poder hacerlo: "El mejor partido estadísticamente ha sido Andrés, pero ha habido algunos jugadores que no han hecho tanto estadísticamente y los pongo muy en valor. En ataque Feliz muy bien, pero necesitamos que mejore igualmente en defensa, él y todos", aseguró en Movistar +.

articles.title: AJ Dybantsa Injured, Latest on Wizards Star's Timeline to Return Ahead of NBA Season Opener
articles.summary: Washington Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa suffered a sprained ankle six days before he is scheduled to make his regular-season NBA debut.
articles.body:
Washington Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa suffered a sprained ankle six days before he is scheduled to make his regular-season NBA debut.

Wizards coach Brian Keefe provided the injury update Friday to sideline reporter Chase Hughes (h/t ESPN ).

"AJ's got an ankle sprain. We just took him out of the game for a precaution," Keefe told reporters after the game. "We'll look at it more, get more information when we get back."

Dybantsa appeared to roll his left ankle in the second quarter of Friday's preseason loss at the New Orleans Pelicans. He had recorded 12 points in 15 minutes of play before exiting the game.

The Wizards are preparing to open the regular season Wednesday against the visiting Milwaukee Bucks.

The 19-year-old was helped up by teammates before limping off the court and sitting out the rest of the game.

Dybantsa finished the preseason having appeared in four exibition games for the Wizards, averaging 12.8 points in 21.5 minutes per game on the court thanks to 44.3 percent shooting from the field.

The Wizards haven't made the playoffs since 2021. Washington has recorded 18 or fewer wins in each of the last three seasons, a span during which Bub Carrington recently said his team was "held back" by trying to secure high draft picks.

Washington selected Alex Sarr with the 2024 No. 2 pick, then drafted Tre Johnson at No. 6 in 2025 before securing former BYU star Dybantsa with the top selection of the 2026 draft.

The Wizards are hoping to finally take the next step after adding Trae Young, Anthony Davis and Khris Middleton to surround their young core. Dybantsa recently told 7News' Scott Abraham (h/t 7News' Aidan Currie ) the Wizards are "trying to make it to the playoffs" this season.

"Teams or fans looking in from the outside are like, 'It's just the Wizards' — which we're totally cool with... We're cool being the underdog, and we'll gun for these other teams," Dybantsa told Abraham.

The Wizards will hope to get good news about Dybantsa as the franchise looks to remain optimistic about beginning a more competitive season next week.

articles.title: Bertomeu, tajante sobre la propuesta de la NBA: "Sería un retroceso"
articles.standfirst: El director ejecutivo de la Euroliga entre 2000 y 2022 cuestiona las condiciones financieras que ofrece y advierte sobre el peligro de sacrificar la identidad del baloncesto europeo.
articles.summary: El director ejecutivo de la Euroliga entre 2000 y 2022 cuestiona las condiciones financieras que ofrece y advierte sobre el peligro de sacrificar la identidad del baloncesto europeo.
articles.body: Jordi Bertomeu, quien fue director ejecutivo de la Euroliga desde 2000 hasta 2022 expresó su preocupación por la propuesta de entrada de la NBA en el baloncesto europeo, argumentando que los términos que se están discutiendo socavarían la independencia de los clubes y pondrían en riesgo las tradiciones de este deporte. Lo hizo en declaraciones al programa Tu diràs de RAC1 que recoge Eurohoops, en las que contrastó la propuesta actual con sus propias gestiones con la liga estadounidense. “Las conversaciones que mantuve con la NBA —debido a la buena relación que teníamos y a que habíamos colaborado en muchos proyectos— giraban en torno a la cooperación”, afirmó. “Tal como se ha presentado, resulta preocupante. Por lo que vemos, es difícil vislumbrar algo positivo para el baloncesto europeo”. Su principal objeción se refiere al control de la competición. Bertomeu recordó que la Euroliga se creó para permitir que los clubes decidieran su propio futuro tras separarse de la FIBA: “Durante 26 años, los clubes han decidido su propio futuro. Ha habido éxitos y errores, incluidos los nuestros, los de quienes lo gestionamos, pero los clubes han sido los propietarios y quienes han decidido cómo funciona su competición”. En opinión de Bertomeu, la oferta de la NBA revertiría esa independencia y devolvería a los clubes a una posición de sumisión ante una autoridad externa. “La propuesta de la NBA pone fin a todo esto y nos hace volver al principio, al punto de partida. Ahora se llama NBA; antes se llamaba FIBA. Pero, en definitiva, los clubes volverían a hacer lo que otros les digan. Me preocupa, y creo que representa un retroceso muy significativo”. Bertomeu recalcó que la expansión a nuevos mercados no era motivo de preocupación en sí misma, y recordó la participación de Londres en los inicios de la Euroliga. Sin embargo, advirtió sobre el peligro de hacerlo a expensas de los clubes ya establecidos. “La NBA no inventó llevar la competición europea a esos lugares, y eso ya es algo bueno en sí mismo. Lo que me preocupa es que esto ocurra a costa del Olympiacos , los equipos de Belgrado, el Zalgiris , el Maccabi , clubes que han contribuido a forjar el baloncesto europeo”. También cuestionó las condiciones financieras, citando cifras que sugerían que los clubes tendrían que pagar considerablemente más para participar de lo que recibirían según el acuerdo propuesto. “Que el Barça, el Olympiacos o el Real Madrid tengan que pagar para jugar en una cancha que ellos mismos han construido no me parece lógico ni razonable. Y lo que me parece absolutamente inaceptable es que, por permitir que esto suceda, reciban una cantidad que es una décima parte de lo que tendrían que pagar posteriormente”. Más allá de la gobernanza y las finanzas, Bertomeu destacó una diferencia fundamental en la cultura deportiva. “Aquí practicamos deporte e intentamos hacer negocios para mantenerlo. Allí, es un negocio que utiliza el deporte como instrumento para hacer negocios. Es una cultura radicalmente diferente. No voy a decir cuál es mejor o peor, pero nuestros equipos, nuestros clubes y nuestros aficionados están claramente acostumbrados a la tensión competitiva, no a la tensión empresarial”. El exdirectivo también expresó dudas sobre el calendario propuesto, al tiempo que reconoció que había ayudado a establecer la Euroliga en tan solo tres meses. "El nivel de sofisticación que tiene hoy la Euroliga, que no tenía en el año 2000, probablemente hace inviable un inicio en 2027", afirmó. "Creo que la fecha de 2027 también se está utilizando para mantener la presión sobre los inversores".

articles.title: LeBron James describes helicopter commute from New York to Philadelphia as 'just another way of transportation'
articles.summary: James' helicopter arrangement is reportedly part of his deal with Fanatics.
articles.body:
LeBron James has been commuting from New York to Philadelphia 76ers practices and games. And he's been doing so by helicopter.

"Yeah, I've done it before," the 41-year-old James said, via ESPN's Kris Rhim , when asked about the arrangement after the Sixers' preseason finale on Friday.

"Just another way of transportation. Yeah, that's all."

While James spoke about his travel setup for the first time in the wake of a 125-120 overtime loss to the Boston Celtics, it's been a topic of conversation for a while. After all, he's one of the basketball greats, and he's playing in his NBA-record-extending 24th season .

Front Office Sports reported earlier this month that James flying back and forth from New York to Philly is part of his deal with Fanatics, a sports platform known for its apparel business. James has been using the company's aviation, a privilege afforded to him after he signed a multi-year trading card partnership with Fanatics in January 2024, according to the Oct. 5 FOS report.

James' travel time is more than halved when he flies by helicopter, compared to driving from New York to Philly. It's estimated to take him between 30 and 45 minutes.

"The deal we signed with Fanatics almost three years ago includes access to their corporate aviation," a spokesperson for James told FOS. "It's a feature in many of their deals with their largest athletes and we appreciate their partnership as LeBron splits his time between New York and Philadelphia."

Although James has promoted Fanatics for years through his partnership with the company, his helicopter perk has been stirring up conversation due to his current NBA situation.

After leaving the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency, James signed a team-friendly deal with the Sixers, more specifically a two-year contract reportedly worth only $8 million. Fanatics, notably, is owned by Michael Rubin, who sold his shares of Sixers ownership in 2022.

At this point, any perceived conflict of interest seems to be the result of conjecture, but investigative journalist Pablo Torre told FOS recently that he and his team were "looking into all of the ways that is both a good story as well as something that is of interest to the league."

He added: "And, by the way, it may not be the latter; it does appear to be the former as a business story."

Torre then released an episode of his show, "Pablo Torre Finds Out," on Thursday addressing the subject. Torre dove into the details surrounding the Fanatics helicopter in question and noted that he had been told league sources have wondered whether Rubin convinced James to sign with the Sixers at Fanatics Fest in mid-July .

But Torre went on to say, "This is not me alleging this is cap circumvention; it is, though, me pointing out, this is pretty funny."

He continued: "It is a pretty funny series of apparent coincidences for a helicopter that lots of people have been asking questions about."

It's possible the hoopla is much ado about nothing. James' tone when answering the question about his helicopter rides on Friday certainly suggests he thinks so.

The Sixers' regular season begins on Tuesday in New York, as James and Co. will take on the defending NBA champion Knicks in Madison Square Garden.

articles.title: Shawn Marion delivers sobering Kyrie Irving reality check amid Mavericks comeback hopes
articles.summary: As Kyrie Irving prepares to return to the Dallas Mavericks for the 2026-27 NBA season after missing the entire previous campaign with a torn ACL, former team...
articles.body:
As Kyrie Irving prepares to return to the Dallas Mavericks for the 2026-27 NBA season after missing the entire previous campaign with a torn ACL, former teammate Shawn Marion delivered a sobering assessment of the star guard's chances of returning to his previous form.

Speaking with Kyle Odegard of Action Network, Marion acknowledged the uncertainty surrounding Irving's comeback, particularly as the 34-year-old prepares to compete in a league featuring younger talent.

"I would like to see him back to that top level. You just don't know, man. The league is so young and everyone is so talented. I want to see what happens, and how he helps the team."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Irving has not appeared in a regular-season game since suffering a torn ACL against the Sacramento Kings in March 2025 . His extended absence raises questions about whether he can immediately regain the scoring ability and explosiveness that made him one of the NBA's premier offensive guards.

Nevertheless, Marion offered an encouraging assessment of Irving's physical condition and preparation throughout his recovery.

"He's been working out like crazy with his teammates and doing his little circuit. He looks good, looks healthy. He could have come back last year but they waited the full year."

Kyrie Irving looks to regain All-Star form with Mavericks after ACL tear

Before his injury, Irving remained one of Dallas' most productive players.

During the 2024-25 season, the nine-time All-Star averaged 24.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.3 steals while shooting 47.3% from the field and 40.1% from 3-point range across 50 appearances. He also averaged 36.1 minutes per game.

The previous season, Irving averaged 25.6 points, 5.2 assists and 5.0 rebounds while shooting 49.7% from the field and 41.1% from beyond the arc in 58 games. His production helped Dallas reach the 2024 NBA Finals .

Now, Irving faces the challenge of returning to that level while adjusting to a significantly different Mavericks roster.

Dallas enters the 2026-27 season hoping to rebound from a disappointing 26-56 campaign that left the franchise 12th in the Western Conference standings.

The Mavericks also struggled throughout their preseason schedule, finishing 1-3 following Friday night's 135-111 loss to the Atlanta Hawks.

Irving's return could provide a significant offensive boost alongside reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg as Dallas attempts to establish consistency under new head coach Dusty May .

However, Marion's comments underscore the uncertainty surrounding Irving's ability to regain his previous production following such a lengthy absence.

The Mavericks will begin their regular season Wednesday, Oct. 21, against the Houston Rockets at 8:30 p.m. ET, giving Irving his first opportunity to demonstrate how much of his All-Star form remains.

Kevin Durant is seemingly unhappy Phoenix Suns owner Mat Ishbia described trading for him in 2023 as part of a failed strategy of throwing "money at the problem."

"#blameKD even though KD stayed on top of his game at 36 and got u back this 'culture' you love so much," Durant wrote Saturday on X. "Aye, Matthew acts like I got arrested for a DUI or sumn."

Ishbia, who completed his purchase of the Suns in February 2023, spoke about the Durant trade made later that month in a recent appearance on CNBC Sport .

"There was not a defined culture and North Star where we were going, and therefore bringing in super talented players like Kevin Durant doesn't necessarily lead to championships," Ishbia said. "You've got to find guys and people that are aligned with the vision of where we're going, the work ethic, the attitude, the care factor around winning, the grind every single day."

Durant ultimately spent two and a half seasons with the Suns before he was traded to the Houston Rockets in July 2025.

articles.standfirst: El exterior malagueño (31) y Brazdeikis (12+7+3) brillan ante el Kids&Us de Oriola (17+6)
articles.summary: El exterior malagueño (31) y Brazdeikis (12+7+3) brillan ante el Kids&Us de Oriola (17+6)
articles.body: El Unicaja se llevó una trabajada victoria del Nou Congost ante un Kids&Us Manresa que nunca dejó de competir (72-84). El conjunto malagueño mandó durante buena parte del encuentro gracias a su intensidad y ritmo, aunque tuvo que sufrir en la segunda mitad ante la reacción local. En ese escenario apareció la figura de Cameron Hunt, decisivo para sostener al equipo y cerrar el triunfo con 31 puntos y 29 de valoración. El conjunto de Txus Vidorreta tomó la iniciativa desde el comienzo. Hunt asumió pronto protagonismo ofensivo y un 2+1 de Kendrick Perry permitió al Unicaja ponerse por delante. El Manresa intentó responder a través de Oriola, aprovechando además algunas pérdidas visitantes, pero los malagueños consiguieron llegar al final del primer cuarto con una renta de seis puntos (16-22). El segundo periodo permitió al Unicaja abrir una brecha importante. Hunt y Lukosius ampliaron la diferencia hasta los once puntos y, pese a que el ritmo anotador descendió, los cajistas siguieron controlando el partido. Brazdeikis, muy activo, firmó un 2+1 y Hunt volvió a aparecer para llevar la ventaja hasta los 18 puntos. El Manresa reaccionó en los últimos minutos antes del descanso y redujo la desventaja hasta el 35-48. Tras el paso por vestuarios, el equipo local encontró nuevas vías para meterse en el partido. Hunt respondió con un triple, pero Notae y Agbo lideraron la ofensiva del Manresa, que llegó a colocarse a solo seis puntos. El Unicaja necesitaba frenar el impulso local y volvió a encontrar a Hunt, autor de cuatro puntos consecutivos que devolvieron cierta tranquilidad. Sin embargo, un nuevo parcial de 6-0 dejó todo abierto al final del tercer cuarto (57-64). El último periodo comenzó con el Manresa dispuesto a completar la remontada. Los locales llegaron a situarse a siete puntos, pero entonces aparecieron de nuevo Brazdeikis y Hunt para devolver al Unicaja una renta de dos dígitos. El conjunto catalán no bajó los brazos y recortó diferencias, aunque Perry y Willy Hernangómez asumieron responsabilidad desde la línea de tiros libres. Con el partido todavía abierto, Hunt volvió a aparecer en el momento decisivo. Su triple terminó de apagar la reacción del Manresa y permitió al Unicaja afrontar los últimos segundos con el triunfo prácticamente asegurado. El 72-84 certificó una victoria trabajada en la que el escolta estadounidense fue el gran protagonista. 72 - Kids&Us Manresa (16+19+22+15): Benitez (12), Notae (13), Agbo (8), Minchev (5), Ongenda (7) -cinco inicial-; Vila (2), Beaufort (-), Bassas (2), Tamba (3), Fernández (3) y Oriola (17). 84 - Unicaja Málaga (22+26+16+20): Pantzar (4), Hunt (31), Brazdeikis (12), Noua (7), Kravish (3) -cinco inicial-; Kalinoski (8), Barreiro (2), Lukosius (3), Djedovic (-), Hernangómez (4) y Perry (10). Árbitros: Martín Caballero, Vicente Martínez e Igor Esteve. Sin eliminados. articles.title: El MoraBanc Andorra tumba al invicto Río Breogán y se estrena
articles.standfirst: Un gran Kuric (26 puntos con 4/8 triples), Akinjo (13+4+10) y Best (17+4+2) lideran el triunfo de los del Principado
articles.summary: Un gran Kuric (26 puntos con 4/8 triples), Akinjo (13+4+10) y Best (17+4+2) lideran el triunfo de los del Principado
articles.body: El MoraBanc Andorra, con un espectacular Kyle Kuric con 26 puntos y 28 de valoración, lideró el primer triunfo de los de Žan Tabak en este inicio de temporada y provocó la primera derrota del Río Breogán de Lugo (108-102), pese al buen encuentro de Francis Alonso, que anotó 24 puntos. El Río Breogán Lugo, el máximo anotador de la Liga ACB en estás tres primeras jornadas, marcó territorio contra un MoraBanc indolente. En el segundo cuarto, la mejora de los de Žan Tabak, al menos a nivel ofensivo, despertó a los locales. Los puntos de Aaron Best con dos triples seguidos sólo acercaron al MoraBanc a 8 puntos con el 40-48. Aún así, los de Luis Casimiro, menos acertados, no se dejaron sorprender y aunque perdieron el parcial de este segundo cuarto se fueron al descanso con un 43-53, con los 13 puntos de Andrić como el más destacado. Un parcial de 14-2 en el inicio del tercer cuarto provocó la remontada parcial del MoraBanc con el 59-58. Y a partir de entonces, apareció el serbio Aleksandar Aranitović anotando 9 puntos seguidos para la reacción de los de Luis Casimiro a 3'26" del final del tercer acto, con 65-70. Los de Tabak lucharon como gato panza arriba y no se dejaron ir pese a las rachas de los lucenses. De un triple de Tevin Brown agotando la posesión y por tablero se pasó al triple de Aaron Best para dejar el 76-78 y con 33 puntos de los locales en este cuarto. Los de Tabak creyeron en la victoria y más con el parcial de 11-3 con seis puntos de 'Cam' McGriff y un triple de Kyle Kuric para situar el 87-81 a 7 minutos del final del partido. articles.title: Histórico Río Breogán: primer equipo que supera los 100 puntos en las cuatro primeras jornadas
articles.standfirst: Nadie en la ACB había arrancado con esa anotación tan alta, récord que los lucenses establecen pese a perder en Andorra
articles.summary: Nadie en la ACB había arrancado con esa anotación tan alta, récord que los lucenses establecen pese a perder en Andorra
articles.body: El Río Breogán es el primer equipo en la historia de la ACB que supera los 100 puntos en cada uno de sus cuatro primeros partidos de Liga, después de firmar 102 este sábado en la pista del Morabanc Andorra, donde sufrió su primera derrota. Había que remontarse 41 años atrás para encontrar el único precedente de un equipo que empezó una campaña de Liga Endesa con tres actuaciones de 100+ tantos. Fue el Real Madrid de Lolo Sáinz en la temporada 1985-86, que llegó al centenar de puntos en las primeras tres jornadas. En la cuarta, no obstante, se quedó en 99 en Valladolid contra el Forum. Ese registro lo superó esta noche el Breogán de Luis Casimiro, que había empezado la temporada logrando 110 puntos ante el Joventut, 101 en Manresa y 115 ante el Girona. Esta noche alcanzó los 102 con un triple del estadounidense Rasir Bolton en la recta final del encuentro.

articles.body: El Obradoiro asaltó este sábado el Coliseum y ganó a San Pablo Burgos por 72-79 pese a una reacción en el último cuarto del equipo local que le permitió reducir una desventaja de catorce puntos a solo dos. El equipo de Porfi Fisac, impulsado por Steward y Doumbouya, firmó un parcial de 12-0 que reabrió el partido, pero los gallegos resistieron y resolvieron el encuentro en el tramo final. El partido comenzó con alternativas para ambos equipos, pero dos triples de Steward impulsaron al San Pablo hasta el 8-5 y Obradoiro respondió con un parcial de 0-7 muy acertado desde el triple. La aportación de Koprivica y los puntos de Guerrero y Doumbouya permitieron recuperar brevemente la ventaja local (23-22), antes de que un triple de Barrueta cerrase el primer periodo con 23-25. Quintela anotó cinco puntos consecutivos al inicio del segundo cuarto y los triples de Barrueta y Brito ampliaron la diferencia hasta el 28-36, obligando a Porfi Fisac a pedir tiempo muerto y Audige acercó a los burgaleses con cuatro tantos seguidos (32-36). Sin embargo, dos triples de Barcello ensancharon de nuevo la diferencia y Abogidi elevó el marcador al 35-45 y provocó otro tiempo muerto local, antes de que Agada estableciese la máxima ventaja gallega (+11). Koprivica respondió con los tres últimos puntos de la primera mitad para dejar al San Pablo a ocho al intermedio. La segunda mitad comenzó con un triple de Steward, aunque Childress mantuvo la ventaja gallega. El San Pablo encontró después soluciones con Samar y Doumbouya y redujo la distancia hasta el 52-55, sin embargo, un triple de Meindl frenó ese acercamiento y el Obradoiro cerró el tercer cuarto con 54-66, apoyado en las aportaciones de Dos Anjos, Agada y Barrueta. Una nueva canasta de Barrueta elevó la renta visitante a catorce puntos al inicio del último periodo (54-68). Fue entonces cuando apareció la mejor reacción burgalesa, Steward abrió un parcial de 12-0 en el que Doumbouya anotó seis puntos, acompañado por las aportaciones de Audige y Sengfelder, para situar el 66-68. El Obradoiro encontró respuesta en Barcello y Soriano, que devolvieron aire a los gallegos y Steward acercó otra vez al San Pablo (68-72), pero un triple de Barrueta puso el 68-75 y complicó la remontada. articles.title: New Knicks Rumors Update James Wiseman, Bruce Brown Roster Competition Ahead of NBA Season
articles.summary: The New York Knicks waived veteran guard Bruce Brown on Saturday, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks waived veteran guard Bruce Brown on Saturday, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Charania noted that center James Wiseman is now set to earn a spot on the Knicks' regular-season roster as a depth piece.

New York has two open roster spots, but could only keep one player in order to avoid crossing into the second apron (h/t ESPN's Bobby Marks ).

Wiseman was competing with fellow big men Drew Eubanks and Tony Bradley for the reserve center role behind Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond, although his path towards a spot on the roster became clearer after Eubanks and Bradley were waived on Thursday.

SNY's Ian Begley previously reported that there was "strong support" within the Knidks "to add Brown as well" as Wiseman, but a trade would have been required to keep him. A deal never materialized prior to his reported release.

As for Wiseman, the No. 2 overall pick in the 2020 NBA draft has been plagued by injuries and inconsistency throughout his tenure in the association.

Still, he's just 25 years old and is coming off a preseason with New York in which he averaged 8.0 points and 4.3 rebounds in 11.5 minutes per game while shooting 81.3 percent from the field.

Wiseman also has some familiarity with Knicks head coach Mike Brown, as Brown previously served as an assistant coach for the Golden State Warriors when the center was a member of the organization.

New York will begin its 2026-27 season as the defending champions during a matchup with the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday. Tip-off is at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Megan Eugenio Crowns Collin Murray-Boyles Toronto’s Next Star: “He’s Gonna Bring The Toronto Raptors What It Was In 2019”
articles.summary: Toronto Raptors rookie Collin Murray-Boyles has earned the admiration of an unexpected fan: a TikTok celebrity who supports the New York Knicks. In a recent...
articles.body:
Toronto Raptors rookie Collin Murray-Boyles has earned the admiration of an unexpected fan: a TikTok celebrity who supports the New York Knicks.

In a recent installment of her popular Minute Madness segment, Megan Eugenio expressed her admiration for the forward, calling him a future All-Star and a leader of Toronto's next championship team. In the video, Eugenio also expressed surprise at how attractive women from different countries find him.

"Collin Murray-Boyles. Three names, 'cause he's sinking threes from behind the arc," Eugenio says. "He was 2 for 2 last game against the New York Knicks, where, granted, they beat us terribly. The Toronto Raptors. It is preseason. We don't have all our people. They don't have all their people. But he scored 19 points, and he already has eight tonight against the New York Knicks. Again."

Murray-Boyles, 21, was selected with the ninth pick in the 2025 NBA draft from the University of South Carolina. The 6-foot-7 power forward has shown his high potential and talent in the 2026 preseason, with an impressive balance of versatile defense, an offensive game, and double-digit scoring and rebounding.

However, Eugenio believes he has much more up his sleeve.

"This guy's gonna be the next breakout star," she said. "If I was willing to predict, he's gonna be the next guy that when I walk into a Tim Hortons, he's gonna be the cardboard cutout holding my next seasonal drink. He's gonna get that sponsorship. He's gonna be the guy that everyone's wearing their jersey in, like, two, three, four years."

Murray-Boyles' success is even compared by Eugenio to Kawhi Leonard's, who took the Toronto team to its first NBA championship in 2019.

"I feel like he's gonna be an All-Star. He's gonna bring the Toronto Raptors what it was in 2019, that championship," Eugenio said. "He's gonna be the next Kawhi Leonard. He's got Scottie Barnes by his side. He's got a young energy on the team."

Eugenio also couldn't believe how young the rookie player is, and admitted her other loyalty.

"He's 21 years old. He was born in 2005. I was coherent by 2005," Eugenio said. "And granted, I know I'm a Knicks fan, but this guy, I can't look away from. He's so young, and yet he's gonna be so amazing. I can't wait to see how this game plays out. And that's my Megan Minute Madness of the day."

articles.title: How will the Spurs find NBA Finals redemption? Here's how, step by step.
articles.summary: Express-News columnist Mike Finger offers his season-long predictions for how the 2026-27 NBA season will go for the San Antonio Spurs.
articles.body:
Predictions are fun. Prediction markets are not. With that in mind, we give you our annual sneak preview of the Spurs' next eight months, while disavowing any responsibility for the potential financial ruin of anyone who misuses this information:

Tuesday: Having stewed about the conference finals all summer, a healthy Jalen Williams and a motivated Shai Gilgeous-Alexander ruin the Spurs' opening night. The new San Antonio four-guard starting lineup shows signs of promise but gets pummeled on the boards, and the Thunder win 112-109.

Friday: Houston's Kevin Durant gets loads of fan support on his old college campus in Austin, but looks distracted throughout an 18-point Spurs romp at the Moody Center. In a postgame interview, Durant reveals that Victor Wembanyama made him reevaluate not only his endorsement deal with FanDuel, but also the morality of scoring on a two-on-one fast break.

November 13: In a nationally televised back-and-forth duel with Golden State's Stephen Curry, Dylan Harper posts a career-high 41 points to lift the Spurs to an overtime victory. Draymond Green speaks glowingly of Harper from the end of the Warriors' bench, where he becomes the first active player to livestream a podcast during a game in which he played.

December 9: With Wembanyama nursing a minor injury that keeps him off the floor for 10 days, the Spurs come up short in the NBA Cup semifinals against Nikola Jokic and the Nuggets. Old friend DeMar DeRozan connects for 11 consecutive 15-foot jumpers, mystifying all of the Gen-Z players who did not realize those shots were legal.

December 25: Wembanyama returns to put on a spectacular Christmas Day show in Madison Square Garden against the reigning NBA champions, but it's De'Aaron Fox who gets the biggest moment. In the closing seconds, he once again challenges OG Anunoby, this time swishing a game-winning floater photographed by approximately 739 of Knicks owner James Dolan's hidden cameras.

January 14: A sellout crowd in Accor Arena turns out to shower praise on France's new cultural icon - Keldon Johnson. After a massive dunk over New Orleans' Zion Williamson, the reigning NBA Sixth Man of the Year celebrates the San Antonio blowout by donning his black cowboy hat, chomping on a baguette, and becoming the first professional athlete ever to blast Darius Rucker from a boombox in Paris.

February 13: Two days after a quiet trade deadline at which the Spurs mostly stood pat, Devin Vassell posts his best all-around performance since being moved to the bench, scoring 27 points to beat Orlando. Former San Antonio assistant Sean Sweeney, the Magic head coach, advises Billy Donovan to stay put for a while.

February 21: At the All-Star Game in Phoenix, Wembanyama and Harper both try to encourage their teammates to play some defense, but nobody listens. Miami's Giannis Antetokounmpo is named the game's Most Valuable Player, and during his postgame interview thanks all of the fans who lost their houses on Polymarket.

March 11: When the Philadelphia 76ers make their visit to San Antonio, most of the team stays at a hotel downtown while LeBron James helicopters in from the mansion he purchased for the weekend at Horseshoe Bay. Carter Bryant, assigned to guard James for most of the night, outscores him 23-17 to continue a monthlong surge.

April 11: Having sewn up the top seed in the West, the Spurs rest most of their starters in the regular-season finale against Portland. This enables Tarris Reed Jr., who fared well in several spurts throughout the spring, to grab 33 rebounds, breaking Dennis Rodman's single-game franchise record.

April 26: Led by a team-high 26 points from Tobias Harris, playing just as the Spurs hoped alongside Wembanyama, the Spurs finish off a first-round sweep of Will Hardy's Utah Jazz.

May 12: After being tested by Houston's athletic wings early in the Western Conference semifinals, Harper and Stephon Castle overwhelm the Rockets in a clinching Game 6. Durant, still reevaluating things, wonders aloud if it was moral for Wembanyama to pick on a guy 16 years older than him.

May 29: In the culmination of a Western Conference finals rematch during which Wembanyama accepted his first NBA MVP award, there's a Game 7 between the Spurs and Thunder for the second year in a row. This time it's in San Antonio, and this time both teams are mostly healthy. The Spurs win again.

June 15: In Game 6 of an NBA Finals in which he was booed lustily in three games at Frost Bank Center, Kawhi Leonard is treated even more rudely in Toronto. Looking like every bit the same two-way force as his Spurs predecessor, Castle puts the clamps down on Leonard while Wembanyama and Fox find Finals redemption.

And more than 100 games after Wembanyama lamented having to wait 100 games for this, the Spurs win in six.

articles.title: Valkyries Beat Dream in WNBA Finals Game 1, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Angel Reese, Top Players
articles.summary: Gabby Williams scored a game-high 26 points (including 16 in the second quarter) to lead the Golden State Valkyries to a 68-64 home win over the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
Gabby Williams scored a game-high 26 points (including 16 in the second quarter) to lead the Golden State Valkyries to a 68-64 home win over the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday afternoon.

Here's a look at notable box score stats and highlights from San Francisco's Chase Center.

Atlanta led for most of the game and took a 22-14 lead after one thanks to an 11-0 quarter-closing run. Angel Reese scored half of Atlanta's points at an efficient 5-of-6 clip.

However, Golden State held the halftime edge after outscoring the Dream 28-17 in the second quarter. Valkyries forward Gabby Williams nearly outscored Atlanta by herself in the second quarter.

The third quarter was all Atlanta thanks in part to All-Star guard Allisha Gray, who returned to the lineup after missing nearly three games with an injured ring finger on her left (shooting) hand.

Gray scored six points and added an assist in the third quarter, when Atlanta outscored Golden State 17-9. She capped the quarter with an impressive off-balance two-pointer.

The pattern in this game featured Atlanta and Golden State alternating dominant quarters, so it was the Valkyries' turn in the fourth. Golden State outscored Atlanta 17-8 in the final 10 minutes, including a 7-0 run (all on free throws) in the last 2:15 of regulation. Williams scored six of those points. She also previously hit a clutch shot to cut Atlanta's lead to 62-61.

It's no surprise that the league's top two most efficient defenses played a tough, low-scoring battle. In the end, the Valkyries won a close one.

Golden State will now host Atlanta for Game 2 on Monday at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Angel Reese Says She Wasn't 'Aggressive' Enough in 2nd Half of Dream's WNBA Finals Game 1 Loss
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese wasn't pleased with her second-half performance during the team's 68-64 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on Saturday.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese wasn't pleased with her second-half performance during the team's 68-64 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on Saturday.

"I don't think they really did anything, maybe that was just on me," Reese told reporters after the defeat. "I wasn't aggressive enough with the ball and trying to get the ball and get to my spot. So, definitely going to do a better job of that next game."

Sophie Calls Out 'Dangerous' Angel Plays 🤔

Reese scored 14 points and pulled down 12 rebounds while shooting 5-of-11 from the field, but committed five fouls and turned the ball over four times in the contest.

She also wasn't able to make her presence felt across the final two quarters of the matchup, as she scored all 14 points in the first half. Reese only attempted two shots after halftime.

Valkyries forward Laeticia Amihere only appeared in one playoff game heading into Saturday's action, but spent plenty of time guarding Reese in Game 1.

Amihere recorded five points, five rebounds, one steal and one block in 14 minutes on the floor.

She received praise from Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase for her defense on Reese following the win.

"I thought [Amihere] did a fantastic job with that matchup [on Angel]. LA had great energy; again, she was kind of our insight with this game plan, and so you could tell there was a lot of confidence in her matchup," Nakase said, per SI.com's Grant Young .

"[Amihere] was really key tonight for our success," she added.

As for Reese, her second-half performance was particularly disappointing considering her improved offensive output this year.

She averaged a career-high 16.4 points per game while shooting 45.1 percent from the field during the regular season before recording 18.0 points per game on 43.3/38.5/87.1 shooting splits in her first five playoff appearances.

While the Dream also have Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard leading their offense, Reese's frontcourt production will be key as Atlanta attempts to avoid a 2-0 series deficit.

articles.title: At her last WNBA Finals, commissioner Cathy Engelbert reflects on growth, her successor: 'You have to have very thick skin'
articles.summary: "Legacies are for history books to write," Cathy Engelbert said as she likely addressed the media for the last time as WNBA commissioner.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The fashion choice that will live in infamy is the New York City skyline dress. But the one better associated with Cathy Engelbert, the first commissioner of the WNBA, is the set of high heels featuring logos of 12 WNBA teams.

The footwear was a Christmas gift from her daughter shortly after Engelbert took the job in 2019. She joked over the years they will become a collector's item thanks to expansion, a long-awaited point of progress that should be the first line in her biography.

The league is entirely different than when she opened that shoe box, and so is the title she will hold for only a few more months. Her successor will have to approach it differently to sustain the period of "hypergrowth" she oversaw. Engelbert didn't shy away from that on Saturday ahead of Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, which saw the Valkyries take a 1-0 series lead over the Dream .

The 2026 Finals marked her last state-of-the-league press conference, aptly held in one of the six expansion franchises announced during her tenure. It was three years ago this month that Engelbert announced the Golden State franchise as the first expansion team since 2008, when the Atlanta Dream, their opponent in the Finals, came aboard.

The finale lacked the blanket of anxiety that filled the room a year ago during tense collective bargaining agreement negotiations, and days after she was called out by WNBA Players Association vice president Napheesa Collier.

For the first time in a long time, a calmness settled. There was no tension or questions about her leadership. No probing. No big news or inquiry. Answering a question about how she wants to be remembered in this role, she borrowed from the legends she's sent into retirement over the years.

"Legacies are for history books to write," Engelbert said.

Engelbert became a victim of her own growth. The role outgrew her and what she believed it to be more than seven years ago when she became the first WNBA commissioner. New teams, more partners, improved marketing and supersized interest restructured her job. She seemed to know that.

"It's a little more complex stakeholder group than I understood when I took the job because the league was so small back then," Engelbert said. The next leader, she said, will have to manage that, "as well as obviously build relationships with players and agents."

It sure felt pointed that she mentioned the media at the top of her answer. That aspect of her job responsibilities never came across as one she was fully comfortable with. The friction grew in recent years while an expanded list of national media outlets invested in the W in ways they hadn't since the late 1990s — or, in some cases, ever.

The WNBA Players Association came next in the list. Engelbert oversaw two transformational CBAs in her tenure, including the first within her initial season. The last turned ugly in a way common in men's professional sports, but had yet to be seen in the WNBA. The sides clashed on whether the rhetoric was personal or simply business. The day of her retirement announcement, Engelbert mentioned the toll this job in the public sphere took on her family. The next commissioner needs to have "thick skin," she said.

Agents are a larger part of the equation, with players acquiring them in college after the passage of name, image and likeness. Million-dollar salaries are at stake under the 2026 CBA that passed in March, and players use financial advisers . There is more to negotiate than ever. All teams, as required in the CBA, will need their own practice facilities — another element barely on the radar when Engelbert came aboard.

There is also more sheer infrastructure to manage. The league's official replay center is on track to open in New Jersey for the 2027 season, Engelbert said Saturday. In her tenure, she expanded the front office, taking particular pride in the marketing department. The league liaisons with teams more, she said, to help if and when needed. Just this week, the league, in partnership with the NBA, Atlanta Hawks and TV broadcast partners, helped move the Dream's Finals games into State Farm Arena , where they can seat more than 17,000 versus the 3,500 at their home Gateway Center Arena.

"We weren't doing a lot of that five, six, seven years ago," Engelbert said. "Now we're helping teams start up. We're helping teams evolve."

The WNBA is using the search firm Excel in its commissioner search. Engelbert said again there are internal and external candidates, including ones she has submitted and from other stakeholders.

"The good news is there's people who really want to take on this role, which I think it's great," Engelbert said.

Engelbert said earlier this year she never intended to stay at the helm longer than 3 1/2 years. She was hired from Deloitte to right the business side of a league mired in a narrative that it was nothing more than a red line in the budget that could never make money. In her opening statement on Saturday, Engelbert remarked she never thought she would be standing at the dais talking about "billions" when it came to the W.

"But we're there," she said of the 4 billion viewers (up 28%) on social and digital platforms. The Valkyries became the first team worth an estimated $1 billion. The media rights deal also meets the mark at $3.1 billion, a number that, when signed, was believed to be a lowball.

The shoes from a non-billion-dollar WNBA era never did make a reappearance. They could be called vintage, joining the apparel en vogue this 30th anniversary season. There were myriad successes in Engelbert's tenure . The 17,000 strong in Valkyrie Violet, bopping boom sticks at key junctures of Game 1, are proof. The next leader to continue the trajectory could meet all the qualities Engelbert and stakeholders want. But the commissioner seat of a major sports league is always lukewarm at best.

articles.title: Gabby Williams delivers late as Valkyries shut down Angel Reese, Dream to win WNBA Finals opener
articles.summary: Gabby Williams scored 26 points and hit six clutch free throws as the Golden State Valkyries erased a late deficit to beat the Atlanta Dream in Game 1.
articles.body: SAN FRANCISCO – The Atlanta Dream had a three-point lead with just over three minutes left in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday. They didn't score again. Gabby Williams finished with 26 points and made six free throws in the final 2:15 as the Golden State Valkyries beat the Dream, 68–64, at Chase Center. Golden State closed on a 7–0 run to take a 1–0 series lead after trailing by seven earlier in the fourth quarter. Atlanta scored just eight points in the final frame and didn't make a field goal after Jordin Canada's jumper with 4:23 remaining. The Dream had opportunities to steal the opener on the road. They spent the closing minutes missing one after another. DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT FOR NATIONAL ANTHEM, RETURN SECONDS LATER BEFORE WNBA FINALS Golden State's defense produced one of the biggest sequences with the Valkyries trailing 62–59. Veronica Burton blocked Canada's layup attempt, and Kiah Stokes rejected Angel Reese on the same possession. Tiffany Hayes grabbed the rebound and found Williams for a running layup that cut the deficit to one with 3:22 left. Stokes finished with five blocks. That one helped turn a potential five-point deficit into a one-point game. Rhyne Howard pushed Atlanta's lead back to three with two free throws, but Williams answered with four straight at the line. Her second pair put Golden State ahead 65–64 with 1:18 remaining. Reese twice stole the ball from Williams in the final 1:41, giving Atlanta chances to change the ending. Neither possession produced a point. Allisha Gray missed a layup after the first steal, and Naz Hillmon missed a three after the second. Stokes split two free throws with 23.8 seconds left to make it 66–64. Gray then missed a potential go-ahead three, and Williams made two more free throws with 4.1 seconds remaining to put the game out of reach. Fans let the officials hear it during the closing minutes The Chase Center crowd made its feelings about the officiating clear with repeated, loud chants of "Refs you suck." Through three quarters, Atlanta had attempted 17 free throws to Golden State's 5. The Dream finished 18-for-21 at the line, compared with 11-for-16 for the Valkyries. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE One of the most notable sequences came with 3:12 remaining, when Howard drove to the basket and Burton was called for a foul. Burton went down holding her face and remained on the floor for a while. Officials reviewed the play for a possible hostile act by Howard, but assessed no foul on the Atlanta guard. Howard made both free throws to give the Dream their 64–61 lead. Those turned out to be Atlanta's final points. Less than a minute later, Hayes went down holding her face after attempting a steal, just before Burton blocked Gray's shot. There was no foul call or review on that sequence, and another loud chant followed from the crowd. Reese starts fast before Williams leads Golden State back These teams account for six of the 10 players named to the WNBA's All-Defensive teams, but the first half produced 81 combined points. Reese did much of the early damage. She scored 11 points on 5-for-6 shooting in the first quarter, including nine during Atlanta's 11–0 run to close the period. The Dream turned a 14–11 deficit into a 22–14 lead, with Reese supplying half their points. ANGEL REESE'S WNBA FINALS APPEARANCE AFTER CHICAGO EXIT RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT WINNING MENTALITY But she didn't make another field goal. Reese finished with 14 points and 12 rebounds, scoring all three of her remaining points on second-quarter free throws. Williams took over in the second quarter, scoring all 16 of her first-half points in that period. She shot 6-for-9 and hit three 3-pointers as Golden State outscored Atlanta 28–17 to take a 42–39 halftime lead. "We were sleeping the whole first quarter," Nakase said at the break. She added: "Our defense is terrible right now!" Golden State's offense became the problem in the third quarter. The Valkyries scored just nine points, and Atlanta took a 56–51 lead into the fourth. Gray, who led the Dream with 19 points, made two jumpers in the final two minutes of the third to help Atlanta regain control. The teams combined for just 51 points after halftime, a much better fit for their defensive reputations. Golden State got enough offense from Williams to survive it.
