articles.title: Fans say ‘astronomical' ticket prices are well worth it for Valkyries-Dream WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Hundreds of dollars, thousands in some cases, bought a seat to watch the Valkyries beat the Dream on Saturday. Some fans saw the steep prices as a sign of th...
articles.body:
Women's basketball fans who flocked to Chase Center on Saturday for Game 1 paid the most expensive ticket prices in WNBA Finals history .

The average price of tickets for Saturday's matchup between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream was four times what it was for Game 1 of last year's Finals, according to StubHub. Was it worth it? Fans said yes - and that the prices reflect the sport's growth.

"No one wants to pay high prices for less quality seats," said Donald Taylor, a Dream fan who paid $250 for a seat in the nosebleeds. "But for women's basketball, just from where it was to where it is now, I think it's a great thing."

A decade ago, Taylor guessed, $250 might get you a courtside ticket to some WNBA games - so he sees the pricey tickets as good for the game.

Even during the WNBA semifinals, some fans were able to get upper level tickets for $50.

Taylor, who is from Oakland and lives in Vallejo, supports the Dream because he has been a fan of forward Angel Reese since her days at Louisiana State University.

The Valkyries' more than 12,000 season-ticket holders get first dibs at face-value playoff tickets. Season-ticket plans range from four-game packages to all 22 home games.

Pete and Jody Cordova, who have season tickets to every Valkyries home game, heard that some fellow season-ticket holders have sold their seats for twice the original price.

"Those who aren't season ticket holders look at the pricing and they go, 'Oh, my god, it's astronomical! People are reselling for such a high price,'" Jody Cordova said. "It's true. It is a high price. But those people who have been putting out thousands of dollars throughout the whole entire season are also trying to recoup some of their money back to help pay for their tickets for this season and for next year."

The Cordovas are paying $350 apiece for club level seats at all four possible Finals home games - $2,800 total if the series goes all seven games.

"Looking at the prices online right now, I think it's a great deal," Jody Cordova said. "But it's still expensive."

Liza Culick and Geri Migielicz, a couple from Santa Cruz, have paid between $250 and $450 per game throughout the playoffs. Tickets in the area in the lower bowl where they have season tickets were going for $1,000 or more on the resale market.

"It's a bummer for people who want to come," Culick said. "I feel like a lot of people in our section are season-ticket holders, so they're coming to the games or giving them to friends."

Cyrus Thomas and Sonia Serna were celebrating their one-year anniversary at Saturday's game. As soon as it was confirmed that the Finals would be Valkyries-Dream, Thomas looked on Gametime, a resale platform. He bought two seats in the nosebleeds for $678.

Thomas is from Atlanta and has lived in San Jose since 1989. He wore a Dream jersey but had both a Dream necklace and a Valkyries necklace around his neck. If the Dream weren't in the Finals, he said, he'd be wearing violet.

"I'm big on firsts. There will never be another first game for the Valkyries in the WNBA Finals," Thomas said. "So I'm like, 'Hey, man, splurge, splurge, splurge.'"

articles.title: Valkyries star Gabby Williams takes over in WNBA Finals Game 1 win, shows why 'she's one of the best players in the world'
articles.summary: A day after telling reporters the media has "never respected me," Gabby Williams will be the talk of it, whether she cares about the praise or not.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The Ballhalla crowd left no doubt as to their appreciation. If anyone in the building wondered, they didn't have a second of peace and quiet to give it a first thought, let alone a second.

The more pertinent inquiry would have been whether Chase Center could withstand any more noise once the clock expired on the second-year franchise's first WNBA Finals victory in history . But then Gabby Williams appeared on the big screen, a microphone in front of her moving mouth the only evidence she was speaking. The crowd drowned out the audio, crescendoing into MVP chants as her "I'm just excited to be here" broke through.

The eight-year veteran spent her career overlooked by the masses despite winning back-to-back championships at UConn in 2015 and 2016, and in her own words, underappreciated by the WNBA franchises she played for previously. A day after telling reporters the media has "never respected me," she will be the talk of it, whether she cares about the praise or not. In a series defined by team defense over established individual stars , Game 1 indicated the name to pop at the end will be Gabby.

That's what 26 points — accounting for nearly 40% of the team's offense in a WNBA Finals debut for both team and individual — will do. Williams hit a game-high 3 3-pointers, went 7 of 8 from the free-throw line, and chipped in 4 rebounds, 2 assists and 1 steal to pull the Valkyries to a 1-0 lead over the Atlanta Dream.

It was the Dream's first loss of the postseason and first since Aug. 28, snapping the record 10-game winning streak. They remain winless in what is their fourth WNBA Finals appearance. Game 2 is Monday at Chase Center.

Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase called Williams "one of our closers," an apt descriptor on a team so solidly rooted in defensive team identity that a bucket-getter couldn't stand alone as the singular one. Over the past month, dating back even to the FIBA World Cup, there is a certain name atop the call sheet with increasingly frantic underlines.

"Gabby is one of the best players in the world," Nakase said. "Like, hands down. She's showing that when we need some buckets, she's willing to go out there and get to her spots and take over. I think she's showing it at the perfect time right now, and that's what we need."

The first 7:42 of her Finals career were forgettable. She missed four shot attempts, three from the perimeter, and the Valks fell behind, 22-14. They defensively gave up 11 on an efficient 5 of 6 to Dream engine Angel Reese.

Williams came alive in the second quarter with 16 points, going 6 of 9 and 3 of 5 from the perimeter. Golden State outscored the Dream, 28-17, in the frame with a scorching 68.8% clip from the field. The Dream were 30.8%, with Reese held scoreless on 3 attempts. The halftime lead was a slim 42-39, the exact type of single-possession affair expected.

Another quiet third quarter ceded the lead back to the Dream, 56-51. Williams went 1 of 6 as the only starter to score in the third while the Valks, whose offense is their question mark, shot 16% (4 of 25) from the field.

Williams, as loudly pronounced by Kiah Stokes in the post-game press conference, is a nerd. While Nakase is poring over coverages and schemes and asking players in the late-game huddle if they're in agreement with the plan, Williams is running numbers. How many points are we down? How many possessions to tie the game? What do we need? When do we go?

"It's the best way to kind of take the pressure off things, too, is just to break them down possession by possession," Williams said.

It's how one of the Valkyries' trainers knows she's about to take over, as she's done routinely throughout Golden State's historic run. The answer, less than one minute into the fourth, when Williams subbed out, was seven points. At least three possessions. A few stops. Pressuring the rim. Soon.

She subbed back in at 5:46, the Valks trailing by three points following a steal and score by Kaila Charles on one end and a block of Rhyne Howard on the other. The Valks offense might have fully dried up if not for a tip-in by Stokes off Williams' driving layup that "got the lid off the basket," Williams said.

"Those are the kinds of things that when our shots aren't falling, those are the kinds of plays that are going to win these kinds of games," Williams said.

The day prior, Williams rapped her knuckles on the wooden table at the thought. Yet, that has never been where the Valkyries stake their success. Defense, she said, is where one can take more control. It's what their late-game confidence stems from. It's why Williams isn't the only closer.

In the final 1:19, the Valkyries pulled down five defensive rebounds and flipped a 64-63 deficit into a 68-64 victory. Despite limping and being in physical discomfort after Jordin Canada backed into her knee at 1:45, Williams' crashing the glass started it. Her two free throws from a foul by Angel Reese gave the Valkyries their first lead since 2:58 of the third quarter, when the Valks briefly led by one point. There was not a singular two-minute stretch in which the Valkyries led in Game 1.

"We had the game right where we wanted it because it just came down to getting stops," Williams said. "That's been our bread and butter all season. That's why we harp on it so much because we've built great defensive habits for these moments."

Charles and Stokes each pulled down defensive boards, boxing out league rebounding leader Reese and reaping the benefits of interior fouls. Stokes hit one and Williams added two more for the final cushion, finishing off an eight-point, 6 of 6 fourth quarter. No other Valkyries player finished in double-digits, but in standard fashion, seven scored. Everyone limited the Dream's offense (a season-low 64 points) and flipped their own script, forcing Atlanta into 12 turnovers while scoring 17 off of them.

Nakase will ask more of her players over the next 48 hours heading into Game 2 before the series quickly shifts to Atlanta. (Game 3 is on Wednesday, with merely one travel day separating the games.) Just because they thrive in single-possession victories they can steal late doesn't mean every one in a long series of tweaks will go their way.

"When a game is this close, even a couple of breakdowns can make a difference," her counterpart, Atlanta head coach Karl Smesko, said.

The Valkyries' home-court advantage is one of deep, unbridled appreciation. Earlier this week, Nakase called for a more hostile game plan. Ballhalla became Boohalla, drowning them over the Dream introductions and substitutions.

They, too, were excited to be there. They're wearing the same chip on their shoulder as their team of former bench players crashing the party too early. Nakase urged them to up their level in Game 2, the way she will ask her players to do the same. The series isn't won in an opener. There's more runway for Williams to finish off the job.

images.caption: Gabby Williams celebrates with her team after their Game 1 win over the Dream. (Ezra Shaw via Getty Images)

articles.title: Joel Embiid rejects idea 76ers stars must 'take a back seat' as NBA regular season looms
articles.summary: Joel Embiid scored 27 points in the 76ers' preseason finale and rejected the idea that Philadelphia's star-laden roster needs to sacrifice.
articles.body: The Philadelphia 76ers boast a star-studded roster that has been projected to make a run at the NBA title. Jaylen Brown arrived in Philadelphia as the centerpiece of a blockbuster trade, while LeBron James later chose the Sixers after considering several teams in free agency this offseason. Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid have spent their entire NBA careers in Philadelphia. Some have questioned whether the 76ers can keep all of their stars satisfied this season, but Embiid believes the team can succeed without forcing its stars to make major sacrifices or drastically alter their playing styles. "I'm against the concept of sacrificing," Embiid said after Friday's preseason finale. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat." LEBRON JAMES ADMITS HE NEARLY JOINED THE KNICKS BEFORE JALEN BRUNSON WON THE NBA TITLE WITHOUT HIM Four of Philadelphia’s stars took the court in the 76ers’ preseason finale Friday, while emerging star VJ Edgecombe sat out. The exhibition nonetheless offered a glimpse of what Nick Nurse’s team could look like when the regular season begins next week. Embiid, in particular, looked to already be in midseason form Friday night, finishing with 27 points, eight rebounds and a highlight-reel-worthy dunk. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day." James struck a similar tone to Brown, although neither seemed concerned about the Sixers’ ability to come together. "We're getting there," James said. articles.title: Dillon Brooks Reacts to Durant-Ishbia Exchange, Thanks Suns Gov. for 'Cleaning Up That Stench'
articles.summary: Phoenix Suns wing Dillon Brooks weighed in on the recent social media exchange between Kevin Durant and Suns governor Mat Ishbia.
articles.body:
Phoenix Suns wing Dillon Brooks weighed in on the recent social media exchange between Kevin Durant and Suns governor Mat Ishbia.

"Thanks Matt for cleaning up that stench in the locker room before I came #culture," Brooks wrote in a Saturday post on his Instagram story .

Earlier on Saturday, Durant appeared to take issue with Ishbia describing the team's 2023 trade for the 16-time All-Star as part of a failed strategy of throwing "money at the problem."

It led to a back-and-forth between the two on social media.

Durant was with Phoenix for just over two seasons from 2023-25 until he was traded to the Houston Rockets in exchange for a package that included Brooks.

Ishbia previously discussed the lesson that he learned from initially acquiring Durant during an appearance on CBNC Sport .

"There was not a defined culture and North Star where we were going, and therefore bringing in super talented players like Kevin Durant doesn't necessarily lead to championships," Ishbia said. "You've got to find guys and people that are aligned with the vision of where we're going, the work ethic, the attitude, the care factor around winning, the grind every single day."

"We have to define what we're about in Phoenix, and stick with it, and believe in our vision and our path," he added. "And I didn't do that at the beginning. I just kind of threw money at the problem."

The Suns made an NBA Finals appearance in 2021 and finished with a 64-18 record the following year, eventually falling in the second round of the playoffs.

During the 2022-23 season, they sat at 30-26 before trading for Durant in a blockbuster swap with the Brooklyn Nets.

The Suns would go on to make the playoffs in two of their three seasons with Durant, but never advanced beyond the second round.

Expectations were low for Phoenix heading into its 2025-26 campaign following Durant's departure, but the team posted a 45-37 record before falling in the first round of the playoffs.

Brooks was a key piece of the Suns' rotation last season, averaging a career-high 20.2 points to go along with 3.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.

articles.title: Gabby Williams lidera a las Valkyries a su primer triunfo en la Finales de la WNBA
articles.standfirst: Anota 26 puntos y es decisiva en el tramo final
articles.summary: Anota 26 puntos y es decisiva en el tramo final
articles.body: Inmejorable debut de Gabby Williams y las Golden State Valkyries en las Finales de la WNBA. Con una actuación soberbia, la cuarta mejor de una debutante en las Finales, Williams lideró a su equipo en el primer partido por el título ante las Atlanta Dream, 68-64 en un abarrorado Chase Center con 18.064 espectadores. Las de San Francisco sólo fueron por delante en el partido en los últimos 100 segundos, eligiendo a la perfección su momento. Un parcial de 7-0 en los últimos 2:15 dieron el triunfo a las locales en su primer partido en unas Finales de la NBA. Hay que recordar que las Valkyries son un equipo con tan sólo dos años de vida. Nacida en Reno pero con pasaporte francés (de hecho juega con Francia), Gabby Williams fue la gran protagonista del partido. Anotó 26 puntos, la cuarta mejor cifra para una debutante en las Finales, pero es que seis de esos puntos llegaron en el parcial de 7-0 con el que Golden State se llevó el choque. En esos dos minutos finales, las Atlanta Dream fallaron todos sus tiros, incluyendo cinco triples, mientras que Williams anotó los seis tiros libres que intentó colocando a su equipo al frente del marcador para ganar. "Es muy bonito, pero siento que aún no hemos terminado el trabajo", dijo Williams cuando le preguntaron qué sentía al escuchar a todo el pabellón corear su nombre. "Incluso cuando íbamos por debajo, pensaba que teníamos el partido donde quería", dijo la jugadora del choque ante las Dream. Williams fue la única jugadora de las Valkyries que anotó en dobles dígitos. Tras ella aparece Kiah Stokes con 9 puntos y 7 rebotes. En Atlanta Alisha Gray hizo 19, Angel Reese 14 y Rhyne Howard 12. El segundo partido se disputará también en el Chase Center en la madrugada del martes al miércoles a las 2:00.

articles.title: NBA Rookies Already Looking Like Draft Steals After Preseason
articles.summary: It'll take some time to fully figure out the correct order of the 2026 NBA draft, but several players have already outperformed their billing in preseason play.
articles.body:
It'll take some time to fully figure out the correct order of the 2026 NBA draft, but several players have already outperformed their billing in preseason play.

If these early indications hold up, we'll remember the 2026 draft as much for the talent that came off the board after the lottery as in it.

We won't ignore a couple of late-lottery prospects here, but we'll also hit a few that fell into the 20s. In each case, strong showings during the exhibition season point to real rotation roles and significantly better production than most expected back in June.

Keep an eye on these rookies. They're off to impressive starts that could develop into careers that defy draft slot expectations.

Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors know they're older and less athletic than almost anyone they'll play this season, which is why they "don't want anything passive" from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg.

So far, the No. 11 pick is obliging with plenty of aggression.

Too strong for wings to handle and too quick for bigs to stay in front of, the 6'9", 240-pound Lendeborg is already a matchup nightmare. He's shown an overpowering downhill game in the preseason—one that'll be even more potent if his three-point shot continues to look legitimate.

Capable of grabbing and going on the defensive glass, the Michigan product sees the floor well in transition and is more than happy to create (and finish through) contact. He's already breaking out a "too small" celebration when he converts against players of virtually any size.

Lendeborg racked up 23 points, 10 rebounds and six assists on Oct. 10 against the Kings and looks very much like the Warriors' second-most-important player behind Curry. He provides athletic force and an attacking style the rest of the roster lacks. He's expected to retain his major role as long as he doesn't fall into the trap of deferring to the team's veterans too often.

A gaggle of point guards came off the board in the first 10 picks of the 2026 draft. Oklahoma City Thunder rookie Bennett Stirtz outplayed most of them through his slate of preseason games.

With 61 points and 13 made threes across his first three preseason contests (followed by a ho-hum seven-point night on Oct. 13), the No. 16 pick is on the way to establishing himself as a rotation piece on a contender.

Stirtz's three-point shot feels like an absolute given. The ball comes out of his hands easily. He's shown no hesitation firing on the catch. If the intriguing floaters and running leaners he showed against the New Orleans Pelicans on Oct. 6 are really part of his game, the 6'4" guard might have a more developed arsenal than expected.

Already 23, the Iowa product may have less runway to improve than several younger guards chosen ahead of him. But at the same time, those prospects aren't guaranteed to match the levels of poise and shot-making Stirtz is already showing.

If you don't see glimpses of Pau Gasol in Thunder rookie Aday Mara, you should consider a visit to the optometrist.

The OKC rookie, taken four spots ahead of Stirtz, has been at least as impressive in a more limited role. Mara produced 17 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and four blocks against the Hawks on Oct. 12, just five days after he went 10-of-10 from the field in 25 minutes against the Bucks.

Absurd scoring efficiency is welcome, but Mara's real swing skill might be his passing. Like Gasol, Mara's eyes start scanning the floor before he receives the ball so he can immediately forward it to the right spot. He sees cutters quickly, delivers the rock on time and has access to all the angles because of his 7'3" stature.

Rim protection and a deft scoring touch seem like givens, but the No. 12 pick could make his draft position look ridiculous if his creation skills hold up during the regular season.

A 7-footer who can impact the game as a defender and scorer is one thing, but a big man who can make plays for others is something special.

Every NBA team wants its rookies to outperform their draft position, but the Dallas Mavericks might be the league's most desperate team in that regard.

That's not to say the stakes are high in Dallas, where 40 wins would count as a massive success. But positionally, the Mavs badly need No. 25 pick Sergio de Larrea to pop as a playmaker.

The Spanish import isn't burly enough to avoid being run over on defense. The reliability of his three-point shot will ultimately matter as much as anything, but de Larrea can absolutely put the basketball where it needs to be. He hit rollers for lobs , slipped smooth pocket passes to cutters and whipped the ball ahead in transition, all with a distinctive flair.

If you're into the idea that great passers are born, not made, you have some solid proof in how de Larrea conducts an offense. Everything he does seems intuitive. Feel drives his game as much as thought.

Kyrie Irving is Dallas' most important playmaker for the next 10 weeks. The Mavs got some early signs that de Larrea could hold that title for the next 10 years.

For a squad that found fewer and fewer uses for backup center Luke Kornet as the 2026 postseason wore on, Tarris Reed Jr.'s preseason work has been a welcome relief.

The No. 26 pick may not offer much in the way of scoring, but the San Antonio Spurs don't need him to pile up points. If Reed simply does what he does best by rebounding on both ends and impacting the game with hustle, he could find himself in a rotation role before long.

Reed grabbed 17 boards (eight on the offensive end) in 24 minutes against the Utah Jazz on Oct. 12. That rebound rate is unrealistic for anyone, but Reed's track record suggests he can sustain it more than most. He hauled down 27 boards and scored 31 points to help UConn beat Furman in the first round of the NCAA tournament last March.

Fellow rookie Jayden Quaintance isn't yet cleared for basketball activities while he rehabs a knee injury, so Reed's opportunities to make a difference should persist for a while. If he keeps this up, the Spurs will have no choice but to give him minutes.

articles.title: Jalen Williams' health, Chet Holmgren's resilience among top storylines for OKC Thunder
articles.summary: The OKC Thunder faces a new season with roster changes and questions about their path back to the NBA title. Here are five key storylines.
articles.body:
The OKC Thunder is looking to win its second championship in franchise history this NBA season .

That's the standard for OKC, which won the title in 2025 but lost to the San Antonio Spurs in last year's Western Conference Finals . But the road back to the NBA's mountaintop won't be an easy one.

OKC will be without some familiar faces after trading away Lu Dort , Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe this summer. And it'll face plenty of tough teams, from San Antonio in the West to the reigning champion New York Knicks in the East.

Here are five storylines for OKC entering this season:

OKC Thunder vs New Orleans Pelicans in NBA preseason game in Tulsa

Mark Daigneault has said in the past that he views the starting lineup as just another rotation decision, and that's accurate. But this is a big question nonetheless following OKC's decision to trade away Dort, a full-time starter since 2020.

One option is Cason Wallace , who's best suited to replace Dort as the team's top point-of-attack defender. The 22-year-old guard earned an All-Defensive second-team selection last season while leading the NBA in total steals (150). He's also a threat in transition and a career 37.4% 3-point shooter.

The second option is Ajay Mitchell , who already has a complete game offensively. He can get into the lane and create for himself or others, which would be a dangerous pairing with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Williams . And while he isn't as good of a defender as Wallace, he can still handle some tough assignments.

Last season was a tough one for Williams, who only played in 38 total games while dealing with a nagging right wrist injury and strains in both hamstrings . But don't forget what he did during the previous season.

Williams averaged a career-high 21.6 points. He earned All-NBA third team , All-Defensive second team and All-Star selections. And he helped OKC win its first championship in franchise history, even dropping 40 points in Game 5 of the NBA Finals .

Williams is a strong shot creator, a talented playmaker, a willing rebounder, a versatile defender and a fiery competitor. He can also play alongside stars and role players, making him an invaluable contributor. If he can stay healthy, he completely changes the dynamic and ceiling of this team.

These were Sarah Phipps' best photos around Oklahoma in September 2026

Dort, Wiggins and Joe logged a combined 5,324 minutes last season, including the playoffs. They also brought different things to the table, from Dort's defense to Wiggins' shot creation to Joe's floor spacing.

Replacing that production will be a group effort. Wallace will have to shine as the top point-of-attack defender. Mitchell will have to step up as a shot creator. Jared McCain will have to provide outside shooting. And that continues throughout the roster, as Kenrich Williams will be tasked with contributing on both ends.

The rookies will also get opportunities to contribute, from Aday Mara's rim protection to Bennett Stirtz's shooting to Otega Oweh's defense. It'll be interesting to see how all of that plays out.

Will Chet Holmgren shake off his end to last season?

Overall, Chet Holmgren played really well last season. He averaged career highs of 17.1 points and 8.9 rebounds while earning All-NBA third team , All-Defensive first team and All-Star selections at age 24.

Holmgren also dominated the first two rounds of the playoffs, but that trend didn't continue against San Antonio in the Western Conference Finals. He was too passive, especially in Game 7. He only attempted two shots in 33 minutes.

OKC doesn't need Holmgren to be a 20-points-per-game scorer. It just needs him to capitalize on his opportunities offensively while being an elite player on the other end.

San Antonio isn't the only other contender in the NBA. But it's the one that beat OKC in last year's playoffs, and it's the one with a core young enough to cause problems for years to come.

Having Williams and Mitchell in the mix will be huge. Their ball handling and shot creation will take pressure off of Gilgeous-Alexander. But there are other question marks with this matchup.

Can Holmgren be consistently effective on offense? Can the Thunder find a way to make life difficult for Victor Wembanyama ? Can it slow the Spurs down in transition? The answers will be revealed throughout the course of this season, which starts with a game between these two teams in San Antonio on Oct. 20.

articles.title: Jalen Williams' health, Chet Holmgren's resilience among top storylines for OKC Thunder
articles.summary: The OKC Thunder faces a new season with roster changes and questions about their path back to the NBA title. Here are five key storylines.
articles.body:
The OKC Thunder is looking to win its second championship in franchise history this NBA season .

That's the standard for OKC, which won the title in 2025 but lost to the San Antonio Spurs in last year's Western Conference Finals . But the road back to the NBA's mountaintop won't be an easy one.

OKC will be without some familiar faces after trading away Lu Dort , Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe this summer. And it'll face plenty of tough teams, from San Antonio in the West to the reigning champion New York Knicks in the East.

Here are five storylines for OKC entering this season:

OKC Thunder vs New Orleans Pelicans in NBA preseason game in Tulsa

Mark Daigneault has said in the past that he views the starting lineup as just another rotation decision, and that's accurate. But this is a big question nonetheless following OKC's decision to trade away Dort, a full-time starter since 2020.

One option is Cason Wallace , who's best suited to replace Dort as the team's top point-of-attack defender. The 22-year-old guard earned an All-Defensive second-team selection last season while leading the NBA in total steals (150). He's also a threat in transition and a career 37.4% 3-point shooter.

The second option is Ajay Mitchell , who already has a complete game offensively. He can get into the lane and create for himself or others, which would be a dangerous pairing with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Williams . And while he isn't as good of a defender as Wallace, he can still handle some tough assignments.

Last season was a tough one for Williams, who only played in 38 total games while dealing with a nagging right wrist injury and strains in both hamstrings . But don't forget what he did during the previous season.

Williams averaged a career-high 21.6 points. He earned All-NBA third team , All-Defensive second team and All-Star selections. And he helped OKC win its first championship in franchise history, even dropping 40 points in Game 5 of the NBA Finals .

Williams is a strong shot creator, a talented playmaker, a willing rebounder, a versatile defender and a fiery competitor. He can also play alongside stars and role players, making him an invaluable contributor. If he can stay healthy, he completely changes the dynamic and ceiling of this team.

These were Sarah Phipps' best photos around Oklahoma in September 2026

Dort, Wiggins and Joe logged a combined 5,324 minutes last season, including the playoffs. They also brought different things to the table, from Dort's defense to Wiggins' shot creation to Joe's floor spacing.

Replacing that production will be a group effort. Wallace will have to shine as the top point-of-attack defender. Mitchell will have to step up as a shot creator. Jared McCain will have to provide outside shooting. And that continues throughout the roster, as Kenrich Williams will be tasked with contributing on both ends.

The rookies will also get opportunities to contribute, from Aday Mara's rim protection to Bennett Stirtz's shooting to Otega Oweh's defense. It'll be interesting to see how all of that plays out.

Will Chet Holmgren shake off his end to last season?

Overall, Chet Holmgren played really well last season. He averaged career highs of 17.1 points and 8.9 rebounds while earning All-NBA third team , All-Defensive first team and All-Star selections at age 24.

Holmgren also dominated the first two rounds of the playoffs, but that trend didn't continue against San Antonio in the Western Conference Finals. He was too passive, especially in Game 7. He only attempted two shots in 33 minutes.

OKC doesn't need Holmgren to be a 20-points-per-game scorer. It just needs him to capitalize on his opportunities offensively while being an elite player on the other end.

San Antonio isn't the only other contender in the NBA. But it's the one that beat OKC in last year's playoffs, and it's the one with a core young enough to cause problems for years to come.

Having Williams and Mitchell in the mix will be huge. Their ball handling and shot creation will take pressure off of Gilgeous-Alexander. But there are other question marks with this matchup.

Can Holmgren be consistently effective on offense? Can the Thunder find a way to make life difficult for Victor Wembanyama ? Can it slow the Spurs down in transition? The answers will be revealed throughout the course of this season, which starts with a game between these two teams in San Antonio on Oct. 20.

articles.title: NBA, sportsbooks reportedly agree to ban multiple types of bets
articles.summary: The NBA will no longer allow certain types of bets that would appear to be the lowest-hanging fruit for potential conspirators.
articles.body:
The NBA will no longer allow certain types of bets that would appear to be the lowest-hanging fruit for potential conspirators.

According to The Associated Press, the NBA sent a memo to sportsbook partners on Friday. Gamblers are now banned from combining the under on a single player's statistics into parlays.

The NBA instructed official betting partners, including FanDuel and DraftKings, to stop offering wagers on opening tip winners, specific missed shots by players, and under bets for players projected to participate for under 12 minutes in a contest. Through its contractual agreements, the NBA holds authority to restrict wager offerings at partner sportsbooks, which the league estimates represent more than 99% of the U.S. sports betting market.

The new restrictions follow federal investigations involving NBA players Terry Rozier and Jontay Porter, which featured parlay wagers placed on the unders of individual players.

In a separate memo sent to franchises on Friday, the NBA detailed updated integrity protocols being implemented for the current season. Retired FBI agent and former NFL player Charles Tillman will conduct face-to-face training sessions regarding league gambling policies. Additionally, the NBA is upgrading its internal AI-driven data surveillance system, which is built to identify and probe suspicious betting patterns related to games or events.

The NBA also updated its fan code of conduct to emphasize regulations concerning threats or harassment. The league partnered with Social Protect, an outside service that detects and removes abusive social media posts, and established a text-based hotline for reporting threats.

articles.title: El Madrid desencadena un diluvio de triples para destrozar al Bilbao
articles.standfirst: Los blancos logran 20 canastas de tres, récord del club en un partido de la Liga Endesa
articles.summary: Los blancos logran 20 canastas de tres, récord del club en un partido de la Liga Endesa
articles.body: Dos no pelean si uno no quiere, y el Surne Bilbao no quiso. Al menos en el primer cuarto, cuando el equipo de Jaume Ponsarnau fue un alma en pena, un juguete en manos de un Madrid que trituró a su rival. El partido lo acabó ganando el equipo blanco, 119-84, pero el choque quedó resumido en un primer acto memorable de los de Pedro Martínez. Aunque el rival ayudó y mucho, los primeros 10 minutos del Madrid pueden ser lo más parecido a lo que Pedro Martínez quiere que sea su equipo. Aunque los 12 triples al descanso son excesivos incluso para él: "no se puede mantener esa efectividad todo el partido", dijo el técnico al descanso, el Madrid dio una clase magistral de tiro, juego fluido en ataque, acierto y defensa. Fueron 10 minutos que acabaron con el partido y un prólogo del dilivio de triples (20) que logró el Madrid, su tope en ACB, superando los 19 que logró en 2016 y que repitió en 2017 y en 2018. El 36-13 lo dice todo. Se cimentó en un primer parcial de 8-0 que era una declaración de intenciones de unos y otros. Ponsarnau cambiaba jugadores de cuatro en cuatro. Hubo un momento en el que seguramente le hubiera gustado cambiar a los 12 de la convocatoria. Y mientras, el Madrid, golpeando con todos los jugadores enchufados. 6/8 en triples en el primer cuatro y 6/13 en el segundo. Y 14 asistencias entregadas al descanso. Hay equipos que no llegan a eso en 40 minutos. Y antes de irse a vestuarios, los blancos llegaron a tener 30 de ventaja, 59-29, aunque el marcador se quedó en 62-35 cuando sonaban la bocina del final de la primera parte. El Madrid ya había destrozado a su rival y sólo queba ver en cuántos pedazos lo dejaba. Los blancos trataron de no pisar el freno y en parte lo consiguieron, alcanzando en la segunda mitad los 20 triples que son el tope del Madrid en un partido de la ACB. Un dato, el jugador que menos puntos anotó en los de Martínez fue Tavares, tan sólo 3, en un choque en el que estuvo 10 minutos y apenas se necesitó su poder de intimidación. El que más jugó fue Pradilla con 21 minutos. El choque pedía esa dosificación. La máxima del Madrid llegó a los 41 puntos (107-66) a 3:47 para el final. Hubo momentos muy brillantes de algunos jugadores del Madrid. Llull, en su partido 700, fue el mejor anotador con 19 puntos, Feliz, que sigue en estado de gracia, hizo 14, Maledon y Jones 13 y Sarr 11. Pero por encima de todos estuvo Facundo Campazzo que dio 13 asistencias una de ellas por detrás de la espalda a Llull que el balear convirtió en triple y que puso en pie al público del Movistar Arena.

articles.title: Sergio Llull sigue haciendo historia: 700 partidos en la Liga Endesa
articles.summary: Cuando Sergio Llull saltó a la pista al comienzo del segundo cuarto, se convertía en el sexto jugador de la historia en alcanzar los 700 partidos en la era ACB. Es el máximo de su equipo, pues el liderato de Felipe Reyes descansa en los partidos jugados también con el Estudiantes.
articles.body: Cuando Sergio Llull saltó a la pista al comienzo del segundo cuarto, se convertía en el sexto jugador de la historia en alcanzar los 700 partidos en la era ACB. Es el máximo de su equipo, pues el liderato de Felipe Reyes descansa en los partidos jugados también con el Estudiantes. Y el caso es que Llull logrará esta temporada ser quinto (le quedan sólo cinco para atrapar a Nacho Azofra, 705) y si se le da muy bien la temporada, cuarto (el quinto es Marcelinho Huertas con 735) o tercero (si da caza a Nacho Rodríguez con 737). Más lejos queda Rafa Jofresa, 756 y el citado Reyes, que es el primero con 824. Llull además tuvo una puesta en escena sensacional. Aunque falló sus dos primeros triples, luego anotó dos seguidos, demostrando que quiere aprovechar cada minuto que le dé Pedro Martínez en pista sobre todo en la competición doméstica, donde está entrando en las convocatorias. Los seis puntos anotados al descanso le dejaron además a uno de ser el primer jugador del Real Madrid en alcanzar los 7.000 puntos anotados en la era ACB. Una hazaña que firmaría a 1:12 para el final del tercer cuatro con dos tiros libres anotados. Luego anotaría tres triples más para totalizar 19 puntos en el partido y avanzar por cierto en la lista de los mejores anotadores en la era ACB.

articles.title: La exhibición descomunal de Jassel Pérez catapulta al Girona
articles.standfirst: El dominicano logró 40 puntos, 9/12 en triples, y 42 de valoración
articles.summary: El dominicano logró 40 puntos, 9/12 en triples, y 42 de valoración
articles.body: El FIATC Girona ganó este domingo al Leyma Coruña en Fontajau (110-90) con una exhibición del alero dominicano Jassel Pérez, que firmó 40 puntos, con un 9 de 12 en triples y 42 créditos de valoración. Un parcial en contra de 36-14 en el último cuarto dio condenó al equipo gallego, que cae en puestos de descenso con un balance de una victoria y tres derrotas. El equipo de Moncho Fernández superó las dolorosas derrotas contra el Kosner Baskonia (118-78) y el Río Breogán (115-92) y se aleja así de la zona baja (dos triunfos en 4 jornadas), en un duelo que afrontaba con solo nueve jugadores profesionales. El acierto exterior de Jassel Pérez dinamitó el récord histórico de anotación del Girona en la Liga Endesa, en un partido en el que también brilló David N'Guessan (19 puntos y 25 créditos de valoración). El conjunto de Carles Marco tuvo cinco jugadores con dobles dígitos de anotación, con Lucas Uleckas como principal referente ofensivo (17), pero hincó la rodilla ante Jassel Pérez. El partido empezó con mucha igualdad e intensidad (6-7), entre dos equipos que sabían que el que perdiera caería en descenso, pero el Girona protagonizó la primera escapada con un parcial de 10-2 con siete puntos de N'Guessan (16-9). El Girona elevó su máxima ventaja hasta los diez puntos con un parcial de 9-0 liderado por Pérez (25-15), y luego el Coruña respondió con un 0-8, pero el equipo de Moncho cerró el primer cuarto con un 28-23 a favor tras un primer triple de Andrzej Pluta. Los visitantes intentaron dar un paso adelante con el inicio del segundo período, pero el Girona redobló su superioridad de la mano de N'Guessan y Jassel Pérez. Alimentaron la renta hasta los 13 puntos a base de triples (44-31). El Coruña no quería que los locales se distanciaran, pero no lograba imponer su dominio habitual en el rebote ofensivo y le penalizaban las pérdidas y la falta de acierto en los triples. Aun así, el conjunto de Marco llegó al descanso a solo cinco puntos (53-48). George Conditt y Tomas Dimsa lideraban la resistencia visitante con diez puntos cada uno. El Coruña, guiado por Uleckas, se colocó a un solo punto en el ecuador del tercer cuarto (60-59), contra un rival que podía comenzar a acosar la falta de rotación por las cuatro bajas. Jassel Pérez y N'Guessan, autores de 39 de los primeros 65 puntos locales, imponían su ley, pero Ulecks castigaba a los locales. Paul Jorgensen empató el duelo con un triple (65-65). El Girona respiró con un 9-3, pero el Coruña cerró el tercer período por delante gracias a un parcial de 0-8 (74-76). Era la primera ventaja visitante desde el 6-7. El partido se inclinaba hacia el lado visitante, pero los locales reaccionaron cuando parecían más tocados de la mano del mejor jugador del partido. Jassel Pérez firmó tres triples y capitaneó un parcial de 14-0 en los primeros tres minutos del último cuarto (88-76). Marco tuvo que pedir dos tiempos muertos e introdujo cinco cambios de golpe, pero el duelo estaba sentenciado. El Girona no tuvo rival en el último período (11-1 en asistencias y 12-3 en rebotes) y Fontajau ovacionó la soberbia actuación de Jassel Pérez. 110 - Bàsquet Girona (28+25+21+36): Stenionis (7), McClung (4), Martínez (9), N'Guessan (19), Geben (9) -cinco inicial-; Pluta (11), Jassel Pérez (40), Maric (4), Kunc (7) y Brunot (-). 90 - Leyma Coruña (23+25+28+14): Pacheco (3), Dimsa (10), Uleckas (17), Radoncic (7), Skapintsev (3) -cinco inicial-; Jorgensen (5), Silins (16), Verge Jr (12), Conditt (12), Díaz (5), Jou (-) y Cuevas (-). Árbitros: Serrano, Olivares y Lezcano. Eliminaron al visitante Conditt (m. 37). Incidencias: Partido de la jornada 4 de la Liga Endesa disputado ante 4.578 aficionados en el Pavelló de Fontajau.

articles.standfirst: Gana su primer partido en el Príncipe Felipe con una exhibición ofensiva ante el iLERNA Lleida
articles.summary: Gana su primer partido en el Príncipe Felipe con una exhibición ofensiva ante el iLERNA Lleida
articles.body: El Casademont Zaragoza ha logrado este domingo su primera victoria en el Príncipe Felipe a costa del iLerna Lleida (109-98) y encadena de esta forma su tercera victoria en lo que va de temporada para cerrar a lo grande las Fiestas del Pilar. Los aragoneses han bombardeado a triples a los catalanes en la primera mitad, lo que les ha permitido coger distancia en el descanso, pero en el último cuarto el Lleida ha logrado acercarse gracias a su juego rápido, que ha puesto nervioso al público zaragozano. Jaworski, que encaja genial en el esquema de García de Vitoria, ha empezado el partido a un ritmo endiablado con ocho puntos en tres jugadas, mientras que el Lleida ha respondido de la mano de Mikel Sanz con dos triples para mantener el encuentro igualado. El festival de triples del Casademont, protagonizado por Guillen Vives y Roberts Blumbergs, parecía adelantar a los maños al final del primer cuarto, pero ha sido Darius McGhee el que ha puesto por delante a los ilerdenses con un triple desde el medio campo (22-23). Vives y Trae Bell-Haynes han levantado a la grada con sus jugadas en el segundo cuarto y en cinco minutos el Casademont se ha colocado 14 arriba (40-26) y, con un Lleida muy incómodo, se ha llegado al descanso (60-43). El Casademont, que ha llegado por tercera vez en su historia a los 60 puntos al descanso, ha empezado el tercer cuarto siguiendo el mismo ritmo y el Lleida, mejor plantado defensivamente, ha sido sostenido por las canastas de Sanz. Con los maños en bonus y seis minutos por delante, el Lleida ha podido sacar partido, pero Zacharie Perrin ha estado muy errado en los tiros libres y ha sido un destacado Mark Hughes quien ha recortado distancias para los catalanes (84-74). El último cuarto ha puesto las pilas al Casademont, que ha empleado un juego rápido liderado por Laurynas Birutis y con un activo Nicolás Brussino que les ha permitido alcanzar los 23 puntos de diferencia (97-80). Era el propio Brussino quien, con dos triples, llevaba a la centena de puntos a los maños, que se han estancado en esa cifra y el Lleida, con las vertiginosas posesiones que les definen, ha llegado a acercarse por medio de Melvin Ejim y James Batemon, pero la distancia ya era insalvable (109-98). 109.- Casademont Zaragoza (22+38+24+25): Gabriel Olaseni (2), Trae Bell-Haynes (16), Robert Blumbergs (9), Miguel González (3), Justin Jaworski (23) -cinco inicial- Birutis (18), Vives (14), Homesley (11), Brussino (9) y Fernández (4). 98.- iLerna Lleida (23+20+31+24): James Batemon (16), Daniel García (4), Mark Hughes (17), Zacharie Perrin (17), Mikel Sanz (18) -cinco inicial- Ejim (14), McGhee (7), Kuath (4) y Rodríguez (2). articles.title: Ben Simmons Calls Doc Rivers 'A Piece of S--t' for Controversial Comment with 76ers
articles.summary: Ben Simmons still isn't happy with Doc Rivers five years after the former head coach's controversial comment following the Philadelphia 76ers' loss to the Atlanta Hawks in Game 7 of their second-round playoff series.
articles.body:
Ben Simmons still isn't happy with Doc Rivers five years after the former head coach's controversial comment following the Philadelphia 76ers' loss to the Atlanta Hawks in Game 7 of their second-round playoff series.

"How did I feel? I was like, 'What a piece of s--t,'" Simmons said of Rivers' comment in the new Being Ben documentary, which debuts Sunday on ESPN (h/t Conor Smith of the Philadelphia Inquirer ).

As Smith noted, Rivers was asked if he felt Simmons could be a point guard for a championship team moving forward after struggling against the Hawks.

"I don't know that question or the answer to that right now," the coach said. "So I don't know the answer to that."

In the documentary, Simmons continued and said, "When you have a relationship with somebody and they have your back, I think certain things are supposed to be handled certain ways. But then you also gotta look at it from the side of 'he's got a job.' You know, he's making his money. He ain't trying to lose his job or anything like that. So, when times get tough, people start panicking. People throw people under the bus, and that's just—it's just what happened."

Simmons famously passed on a potential dunk in the late moments of that Game 7 loss and seemed hesitant to shoot throughout the series.

He requested a trade the following offseason, missed the 2021-22 campaign and then played for the Brooklyn Nets and Los Angeles Clippers the following three seasons before taking the 2025-26 season off.

The LSU product has since returned and is a member of the Sacramento Kings.

But his end with the 76ers was an unceremonious one, especially given how promising things seemed to be at the start. He entered the league as the No. 1 overall pick of the 2016 NBA draft, won the Rookie of the Year and was a three-time All-Star in his first four seasons.

He was also a back-to-back All-Defensive First Team selection in 2019-20 and 2020-21 and appeared to be a franchise building block for the 76ers.

Yet the offensive issues, especially in that series, defined the ending of his time with Philadelphia.

articles.title: El Valencia cura sus heridas apalizando al UCAM Murcia
articles.standfirst: Cierra una serie de tres derrotas seguidas regresando a su mejor versión
articles.summary: Cierra una serie de tres derrotas seguidas regresando a su mejor versión
articles.body: La intensidad que mostró el Valencia Basket, tras una dura jornada doble en la Euroliga, y la buena lectura del equipo de Xavi Albert ante las embocadas tácticas que sle planteó desarmaron este domingo al UCAM Murcia, que acabó arrollado en el Roig Arena y se queda con una sola victoria en su casillero en la Liga Endesa frente a las dos del equipo 'taronja' tras cuatro jornadas. El Valencia Basket contó con la inspiración ofensiva de Jasiel Rivero, Armori Brooks, TJ Shorts y Nikola Mirotic pero antes con la intensidad, y algunos puntos más, que le dieron Álvaro Cárdenas, Gonzalo Cortarzar y Neal Sako. Su rival no encontró referentes hasta que, cuando todo estaba perdido, la intensidad de Marcis Steinbergs y el despertar, primero de Dylan Ennis y después de Michael Forrest, le permitieron maquillar el resultado. Dos decisiones marcaron el inicio: la apuesta de Sito Alonso de pasar por detrás el bloqueo a TJ Shorts y concederle tiros a cinco metros y la de Albert de situar sobre Boum primero a Corbalán y más adelante a Cárdenas para cegar al base y contagiar a sus propios compañeros de la intensidad defensiva que le había faltado el jueves ante el Maccabi Tel Aviv. El buen hacer murciano en el rebote de ataque no se traducía en puntos y el técnico visitante pidió un tempranero tiempo para reordenar a los suyos pero el UCAM ya iba por detrás y tuvo que recurrir a una defensa zonal. El Valencia, con el cubano Rivero y Mirotic al poste alto, desactivó también ese recurso y abrió hueco hasta doblar a su rival con un par de triples del montenegrino (34-17, m.12). Viendo que sus ajustes no tenían el efecto, el equipo murciano perdió la fe y la renta local se fue por encima de los veinte puntos, impulsada en la continuidad de su intensidad defensiva. Los puntos de un inspirado Rivero, sumó 12 en sus primeros 8 minutos, y la buena dirección y el desparpajo de Cárdenas eclipsaron la mejoría que encontró el UCAM con el regreso a la defensa individual y el trabajo de Raieste en ambos lados de la pista. El Valencia llegó al descanso con su ventaja intacta y el dominio de las sensaciones (58-36, m.20). No hubo salida en tromba del UCAM tras el parón, en parte, porque enfrente volvieron a turnarse Corbalán y Cárdenas para mantener la intensidad 'taronja' y porque Brooks encontró los espacios para anotar. La renta local se acercaba ya a los treinta puntos pese a que Ennis intentó echarse a su equipo a la espalda (76-49, m.26). Cuando los locales empezaron a levantar el pie, que lo hicieron, la diferencia de confianza entre los jugadores de ambos equipos era tal, que no solo no se reflejó en el marcador sino que la distancia local siguió aumentando. Con el encuentro aparentemente decidido, la intensidad de Steinbergs, que apenas había tenido protagonismo hasta entonces, revivió al UCAM. Sus canastas y sus buenos bloqueos permitieron al equipo pasar del 88-60 al 90-74 con un par de triples de Forrest. Pero TJ Shorts sofocó rápido ese último intento murciano de regresar al choque. Un par de acciones del escurridizo exterior acabaron con la última esperanza visitante y lanzaron al Valencia más allá de la centena de puntos para cerrar sin apuros una cómoda victoria que le permite engancharse al vagón de cabeza de la ACB. 116.- Valencia Basket (25+33+28+30): TJ Shorts (16), Corbalán (6), Taylor (4), Osetkowski (3), Sako (12) -cinco titular- Cárdenas (12), Brooks (16), Saint-Supéry (6), Puerto (3), Mirotic (15), Rivero (20) y Reuvers (3). 93.- UCAM Murcia (14+22+24+33): Boum (14), Radebaugh (3), Raieste (4), Nakic (-), Cate (4) -cinco titular- Forrest (18), Sant-Ross (3), Falk (7), Pansa (4), Diagné (2), Steinbergs (6) y Ennis (28). articles.title: La Laguna da la bienvenida a Perasovic con su primera derrota en la Liga Endesa
articles.standfirst: Los canarios derrotan al Kosner Baskonia en un trabajadísimo partido.
articles.summary: Los canarios derrotan al Kosner Baskonia en un trabajadísimo partido.
articles.body: La Laguna Tenerife derrotó al Kosner Baskonia (82-77) en un partido muy trabajado por parte de los de Jaka Lakovic que, a pesar de verse contra las cuerdas en el tercer cuarto, firmaron unos aguerridos últimos diez minutos para remontar el encuentro y consumar una gran victoria. La Laguna Tenerife quería alargar la buena racha de resultados y sensaciones y así lo demostró desde el comienzo de este nuevo choque en su feudo,dominando en el primer cuarto a pesar de que Baskonia ofreció un buen papel y se mantuvo siempre en el hilo del encuentro, con no más de dos o tres puntos de diferencia en los primeros siete minutos. A partir de ese momento los aurinegros apretaron el acelerador y llegaron a ponerse siete arriba (21-14) a falta de poco más de dos minutos para el cierre del primer cuarto, que finalmente concluyó con un 25-18 favorable a los locales. Para el segundo cuarto, los de Velimir Perasovic quisieron voltear las tornas y firmaron unos primeros minutos muy serios en los que recortaron la distancia a solo un punto, sin dejar que los isleños anotaran ningún punto (25-24), lo que encendió las alarmas en el cuerpo técnico de Lakovic, que se vio obligado a pedir tiempo muerto para cortar la buena dinámica del Baskonia, y lo terminaría consiguiendo gracias al triple de Fitipaldo nada más regresar del pequeño parón (28-24). Aún así, el conjunto vitoriano no se dejó amedrentar y realizó un arduo trabajo de concentración y dominio de la presión que estaba sometiendo el Santiago Martín, para seguir recortando distancias hasta el minuto 18, en el que materializaron por primera vez en el encuentro la remontada al combinado canarista (34-36), aunque los locales lograron salvar los papeles antes del descanso con un triple de Van Beck en el último segundo (39-36). Para la segunda parte, Perasovic pareció haber dado con la tecla necesaria y el Baskonia asedió a La Laguna Tenerife, dominando con contundencia el tercer tiempo en el que no sólo volvieron a darle la vuelta al partido, sino que implantaron la sensación de que los locales no iban a poder reponerse. Eso fue algo palpable en situaciones como la que se vivió en el último minuto, en el que los tinerfeños se acercaron (52-54), pero rápidamente reaccionó AJ Lawson con dos triples en apenas 40 segundos y cerrar así el tercer cuarto con un 54-60. La Laguna Tenerife no había tenido su última palabra en el choque y en los últimos diez minutos demostraron que el proyecto de Lakovic comienza con fuerza esta campaña 26-27, ya que se vinieron arriba, arropados por su afición, y consumaron una gran remontada que empezó gracias a los cinco puntos de Guy en los dos primeros minutos; y, posteriormente, dos triples de Doornekamp que para igualaron la contienda (65-65). El Baskonia siguió intentando imponer de nuevo el dominio demostrado en el tercer cuarto, pero los aurinegros ya habían tomado la velocidad de crucero que no bajaron hasta la última jugada del partido, con un trabajo defensivo notable, pero una eficiencia ofensiva sobresaliente. Terminaron el último cuarto marcando 28 puntos gracias en parte a un desatado Guy (24 puntos) y Vince Hunter, que ayudaron a los suyos para concluir un peleadísimo encuentro con el 82-77 final. 82; La Laguna Tenerife (25+14+15+28): Guy (24), Fitipaldo (8), Abromaitis (4), Happ (7), Kurucs (2) -inicial-, Fernández (4), Van Beck (6), López-Arostegui (-), Huertas (6), Hunter (15), Alderete (-), Doornekamp (6). 77; Kosner Baskonia (18+18+24+17): Stewart Jr (11), Joksimovic (2), Sedekerkskis (7), Baught (5), Faried (9) -inicial-, Lawson (11), Kurucs (9), Spagnolo (15), Santos (0), Frisch (8). Árbitros: Jordi Aliaga, Joaquín García y Alberto Baena. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la Liga Endesa disputado en el Pabellón Santiago Martín, ante 4.438 aficionados.

articles.title: Paul George Says He Rediscovered 'Love' for Basketball After Being Traded to Celtics from 76ers
articles.summary: Paul George wasn't the headliner in the monster trade that sent Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason, but the veteran is rediscovering his "love" for the game with the Boston Celtics.
articles.body:
Paul George wasn't the headliner in the monster trade that sent Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason, but the veteran is rediscovering his "love" for the game with the Boston Celtics.

"I'm fully immersing myself into this organization with the guys," he told Gary Washburn of the Boston Globe . "I've been more than happy. I'm ecstatic with being here, being around these guys, like they brought something else out of me that to be quite frank has been buried, and that's just a different passion. There's a love again for this game, and I just think everything is kind of just aligning at the right time for me here."

He continued, spotlighting the tradition that comes with being a member of the Celtics.

"This locker room, the culture here, the front office, the city, the organization, the tradition, all of that is something that I've never been a part of," George said. "Where everything is high quality. For me, it's refreshing. Hopefully, I can remain healthy. I think I became a journeyman along the way. At this point, I would love to be able to call Boston home."

George spent his first seven seasons with the Indiana Pacers, so it is somewhat notable to hear him call himself a journeyman at this point.

But he has since played for the Oklahoma City Thunder, Los Angeles Clippers and 76ers with the stint in Philadelphia lasting just two seasons.

Injuries have been an issue for George as well, as he played just 41 games in 2024-25 and 31 games in 2025-26 when he was with the 76ers.

There was a time when he was one of the best two-way players in the league with a resume that includes six All-NBA selections, nine All-Star nods and four All-Defensive selections. While it is unrealistic for the Celtics to expect him to perform like that at 36 years old in what will be his 17th season, it isn't unreasonable to expect him to be a key contributor.

That is especially the case if he is playing with a newfound love for the game.

George also won't be asked to be the primary playmaker on a team with Jayson Tatum leading the way and other playmakers such as Derrick White and Payton Pritchard expected to be key contributors.

That will allow George to take advantage of open space and, ideally for Boston, help it go on a deep playoff run in the Eastern Conference.

articles.title: Ben Simmons Blasts Daryl Morey in Explosive New Comments on End of His 76ers Tenure
articles.summary: Ben Simmons won't be sending Daryl Morey any holiday cards this year.
articles.body:
Ben Simmons won't be sending Daryl Morey any holiday cards this year.

The NBA player and former Philadelphia 76ers star suggested that his holdout and ultimate departure from the Sixers during the 2021-22 season stemmed from the team's former president of basketball operations, Daryl Morey, trying to push him out the door.

"Especially come from up there, up top and upstairs, you're vocally saying you're trying to get me out of there or set things up or whatever. I think at that point—I'm one of those people, like I'm going to show you, you don't want me here? F--k it, I ain't coming in," Simmons said during ESPN's Being Ben documentary. "And that's where it came from. So it was never like I never wanted to be in Philly. Somebody had come in, obviously was trying to get me out, whatever, made promises to James [Harden]. Obviously James and him don't have... I don't believe have a relationship anymore . But that's just the business. There's some good guys in there and some bad guys and some people you can't trust. There's some snakes. And I think he's one of them."

Ben Simmons Calls Doc Rivers 'A Piece of S--t'

Morey had been hired by the Sixers one year prior to Simmons' holdout.

As for the infamous practice Simmons was kicked out of during that ordeal—with conflicting reports regarding whether Simmons had a phone in his pocket during the practice—former head coach Doc Rivers offered more details.

"I think that was way overblown than what it was," he said during an interview on Being Ben . "Ben didn't want to be at the practice, nor did I think he should be at the practice. I didn't even notice the phone. I just noticed he didn't want to be on the floor, didn't want to do anything. But it wasn't some yelling match or anything like that. ... And it wasn't like he was going to fight it. He wanted to go."

Simmons, 30, has played just 108 games over the past five years since departing the Sixers, hampered by injuries. He didn't play at all last season. But he signed with the Sacramento Kings this past offseason and is expected to start for the team in the 2026-27 campaign.
